The code is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/Sangminhong/PrintAnything}{https://github.com/Sangminhong/PrintAnything}.

AI.tldr: PrintAnything is a novel framework that generates 3D printing G-code directly from 3D point clouds without requiring mesh reconstruction. It uses a slice-wise point projection strategy to convert unstructured point clouds into slice-aligned 2D representations and a Geometric plan (G-plan) map (composed of occupancy, region, and flow maps) to encode geometric and extrusion properties for toolpath synthesis, enabling a fully mesh-free 3D printing pipeline.
AI.motivation: Most existing 3D printing pipelines require watertight meshes as input, preventing direct use of point clouds for fabrication. Reconstructing meshes from point clouds often produces geometric artifacts (incorrect faces, topological inconsistencies) that are difficult to repair and can lead to printing failures. A mesh-free approach that directly generates printable G-code from point clouds is needed.
AI.method: The framework introduces (1) a slice-wise point projection strategy that transforms unstructured 3D point clouds into slice-aligned 2D representations matching the layer-by-layer nature of fused deposition modeling, and (2) a Geometric plan (G-plan) map, a compact 2D representation with occupancy, region, and flow maps that encode geometric and extrusion properties required for toolpath synthesis. The system learns to produce executable G-code directly from these representations.
AI.result: The proposed method accurately generates printable G-code directly from point clouds, enabling a practical and fully mesh-free pipeline for 3D printing. The code is publicly available.
AI.conclusion: PrintAnything successfully eliminates mesh dependency in 3D printing by learning to generate executable G-code directly from point clouds via slice-wise projection and G-plan maps, providing a practical fully mesh-free fabrication pipeline.

title: Wiring diagram extraction and gluing: a case study in classifying figure skating jumps using 3D dataset
summary: Hasse clustering is an algorithm that extracts common patterns in sequential data and represents them in graphical forms. As the number of expected clusters grows, however, the algorithm can become infeasible to run due to combinatorial complexity. In this article, we describe a theory of gluing wiring diagrams, allowing iterative applications of Hasse clustering to achieve the same result as a single application. We test our theory in the context of classifying videos of figure skating jumps.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a theory of gluing wiring diagrams that enables iterative applications of Hasse clustering to be equivalent to a single application, addressing the combinatorial complexity that makes Hasse clustering infeasible for large numbers of expected clusters. The approach is validated on a figure skating jump classification task.
AI.motivation: Hasse clustering, which extracts common patterns in sequential data as graphical forms, becomes computationally infeasible as the number of expected clusters grows due to combinatorial complexity. A scalable approach is needed.
AI.method: The paper develops a theory of gluing wiring diagrams that decomposes a single large Hasse clustering problem into multiple smaller, iterative applications that provably produce the same result.
AI.result: The gluing of wiring diagrams theory is tested in the context of classifying videos of figure skating jumps, demonstrating the feasibility of the iterative approach.
AI.conclusion: Gluing wiring diagrams provides a principled way to make Hasse clustering scalable by breaking it into iterative sub-problems without loss of equivalence to the single-pass result.

title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, and 15 tables, including appendices
summary: Scaling coding agents requires a continuing supply of executable data for training, benchmarking, and continuous evaluation. Each task must couple a realistic software state with a specification, development tools, and reliable verification. To expand this supply, we present Change2Task, a system grounded in repository history that converts merged pull requests into verified tasks on healthy modern revisions of the same repository. It aligns historical evidence with evolved code, reconstructs task states through Patch Reversal, Code Mapping, or Agent Reconstruction, and validates the lifecycle from a healthy base to a task state and a restored state. By deriving multiple tasks grounded in developer evidence from maintained environments, Change2Task provides executable data for coding agent training and evaluation while reducing repeated environment setup, storage, and task construction effort. We evaluate the system through five common and widely adopted coding agent task families: Bug Fix, Feature Addition, Test Generation, Application Programming Interface Migration, and Security Repair. Starting from 1,130 source changes eligible for construction, Change2Task achieves 79.6% verified task construction success across these task families. On a matched candidate set, it recovers 29.2% more verified tasks than a construction baseline based on pull requests. Historical and reconstructed cases achieve up to 98.0% matched outcome agreement under agent evaluation, while reuse of modern bases reduces measured expenditure across the complete pipeline by 10.8%.

AI.tldr: Change2Task is a system that converts merged pull requests from repository history into verified executable coding tasks on current, healthy repository revisions. It achieves 79.6% verified task construction success across five task families and recovers 29.2% more verified tasks than a pull-request-based baseline.
AI.motivation: Scaling coding agents requires a continuous supply of executable data for training, benchmarking, and evaluation. Each task must couple realistic software states with specifications, tools, and reliable verification, but constructing such data at scale remains a challenge.
AI.method: Change2Task grounds in repository history, converting merged pull requests into verified tasks on healthy modern revisions. It uses three reconstruction strategies (Patch Reversal, Code Mapping, Agent Reconstruction), aligns historical evidence with evolved code, and validates the full task lifecycle from healthy base to task state to restored state.
AI.result: From 1,130 eligible source changes, Change2Task achieves 79.6% verified task construction success across Bug Fix, Feature Addition, Test Generation, API Migration, and Security Repair families. It recovers 29.2% more verified tasks than a PR-based baseline, achieves up to 98.0% matched outcome agreement under agent evaluation, and reduces pipeline expenditure by 10.8% through reuse of modern bases.
AI.conclusion: Change2Task provides a scalable, verified source of executable coding tasks from maintained environments, reducing repeated environment setup, storage, and task construction effort while improving the supply of quality training and evaluation data for coding agents.

title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Channel Modeling in Low-SNR Regimes
summary: Accurate multipath parameter estimation is critical for modern wireless communication systems, particularly in challenging low-SNR environments. Traditional Maximum Likelihood Estimation algorithms, such as CLEAN, provide high-resolution parameter extraction but suffer from prohibitive computational complexity due to exhaustive grid search. Conversely, purely data-driven deep learning approaches lack physical grounding and struggle to generalize across variable multipath densities and off-grid parameters. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN (NN-CLEAN), a hybrid framework that embeds a multi-head residual network directly into the iterative CLEAN extraction loop. By replacing the exhaustive grid search with rapid, parallelizable forward passes while delegating residual subtraction to exact mathematical models, NN-CLEAN isolates physical multipath parameters without accumulating non- physical errors. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that NN-CLEAN achieves estimation accuracy exceeding 96% at 5 dB SNR, matching the traditional Grid-Search CLEAN (GS- CLEAN) baseline, while providing a massive reduction in computational complexity and substantially outperforming subspace methods and standalone one-shot neural networks. Crucially, NN-CLEAN exhibits a near-flat scaling in execution runtime and memory consumption as batch sizes increase. This highly efficient parallelization establishes NN-CLEAN as a robust, real- time solution for channel estimation in MIMO systems.

AI.tldr: NN-CLEAN is a hybrid framework combining a multi-head residual network with the iterative CLEAN extraction loop for multipath parameter estimation, replacing exhaustive grid search with fast parallel forward passes while using exact mathematical models for residual subtraction. It achieves >96% estimation accuracy at 5 dB SNR—matching Grid-Search CLEAN—with massive computational savings and near-flat runtime/memory scaling versus batch size.
AI.motivation: Traditional Maximum Likelihood Estimation methods (e.g., CLEAN) offer high-resolution multipath parameter extraction but suffer prohibitive computational complexity from exhaustive grid search, while purely data-driven deep learning approaches lack physical grounding and generalize poorly across variable multipath densities and off-grid parameters.
AI.method: NN-CLEAN embeds a multi-head residual network directly into the iterative CLEAN extraction loop, replacing exhaustive grid search with rapid parallelizable forward passes while delegating residual subtraction to exact mathematical models to isolate physical multipath parameters without accumulating non-physical errors.
AI.result: Monte Carlo simulations show NN-CLEAN achieves estimation accuracy exceeding 96% at 5 dB SNR, matching Grid-Search CLEAN, while massively reducing computational complexity and outperforming subspace methods and standalone one-shot neural networks. It also exhibits near-flat scaling in runtime and memory as batch size increases.
AI.conclusion: NN-CLEAN establishes itself as a robust, real-time solution for channel estimation in MIMO systems, leveraging highly efficient parallelization to overcome the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost in multipath parameter estimation.

title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation
summary: Building interactive digital twins requires recovering both 3D geometry and the kinematic structures that govern how objects articulate. Yet existing methods for articulated object reconstruction require explicitly observable motion from multiple articulation states. We introduce a rest-state formulation that reconstructs articulated objects from a single closed configuration, an inherently ill-posed setting where geometry, semantics, and motion priors compensate for the absence of motion cues. Our framework adopts an explicit mesh as an intermediate representation for cross-model verification and fusion, reconciling noisy outputs from vision-language and segmentation models into spatially consistent part structures. To estimate joint parameters without observed motion, we use a video diffusion model to synthesize articulation hypotheses and validate them through geometric consistency. Our approach achieves accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation, performing competitively with motion-observing reconstruction-based, generation-based, and modular pretrained-model baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a rest-state formulation that reconstructs articulated 3D objects from a single closed configuration, using explicit meshes for cross-model fusion and video diffusion models to synthesize and validate articulation hypotheses via geometric consistency.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for articulated object reconstruction require observable motion from multiple articulation states, but many real-world objects are only available in a single closed configuration, making this a fundamentally ill-posed problem that lacks motion cues.
AI.method: The framework uses an explicit mesh as an intermediate representation to reconcile noisy outputs from vision-language and segmentation models into spatially consistent part structures. Joint parameters are estimated without observed motion by using a video diffusion model to synthesize articulation hypotheses, which are then validated through geometric consistency checks.
AI.result: The approach achieves accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation, performing competitively with motion-observing reconstruction-based, generation-based, and modular pretrained-model baselines.
AI.conclusion: Recovering both geometry and kinematic structure from a single closed configuration is feasible by compensating for missing motion cues through a combination of geometry, semantics, motion priors, and cross-model verification via explicit mesh representations.

title: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
summary: Building generalizable agents for diverse applications remains a fundamental challenge. While imitation learning-based policies succeed in specific training environments, they often fail to generalize to novel scenes and tasks. In this work, we propose World Action Planner, a robot planning system that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and the physical grounding of a multi-task pose-image conditioned world model. Our system enables an agent to propose initial action plans and iteratively refine them via optimization and search, reasoning over imagined world model rollouts. We demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance across compositional tasks, new layouts, and zero-shot generalization scenarios, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art end-to-end policy models such as VLAs and WAMs. Project website at worldactionplanner.github.io

AI.tldr: World Action Planner is a robot planning system combining Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with a multi-task pose-image conditioned world model to generate and iteratively refine action plans via optimization and search over imagined rollouts, achieving superior generalization across compositional tasks, new layouts, and zero-shot scenarios compared to state-of-the-art end-to-end policies.
AI.motivation: Imitation learning-based policies succeed in specific training environments but fail to generalize to novel scenes and tasks, limiting their applicability in diverse real-world settings. A more generalizable robot planning approach is needed.
AI.method: The system leverages VLM reasoning capabilities for initial action plan proposal and physical grounding from a multi-task pose-image conditioned world model. Action plans are iteratively refined through optimization and search, reasoning over imagined world model rollouts.
AI.result: The approach achieves superior performance across compositional tasks, new layouts, and zero-shot generalization scenarios, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art end-to-end policy models such as VLAs (Vision-Language-Action models) and WAMs (World Action Models).
AI.conclusion: Combining VLM reasoning with a physically grounded world model for iterative plan refinement provides a robust and generalizable alternative to end-to-end policy learning for robot planning.

title: FADEx: Feature Attribution and Distortion-based Explanation of Dimensionality Reduction
comment: 18 pages, 17 figures, to be published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
summary: Dimensionality Reduction (DR) is a fundamental tool for high-dimensional data exploration, reducing the complexity of latent spaces of machine learning models, and assisting in the explanation of complex opaque models. However, non-linear DR techniques often function as opaque transformations themselves, making it challenging to understand how individual features influence instance positioning in the reduced space. This lack of transparency complicates the analysis and interpretation of structural patterns, hindering the ability to reason about the organization of high-dimensional data based on the projected layout. In order to address this challenge, dimensionality reduction explanation methods have shown promise in improving the understanding of the observed groups and cluster structures. Unfortunately, existing DR explanation approaches tend to suffer from limitations such as multiple attributions per feature and restricted applicability to specific dimensionality reduction methods, which hinder their use. In this work, we propose FADEx, a novel local per-instance feature attribution method that leverages local linear approximation via first-order Taylor expansion and Singular Value Decomposition to provide explanations. FADEx computes the local linear models via weighted least squares, eliminating the need for out-of-sample data mapping, making it agnostic to the DR method, while simultaneously providing local feature attributions and distortion analysis. Through qualitative and quantitative evaluations, comparisons with existing methods, and case studies, we demonstrate FADEx's effectiveness and versatility in providing explanations and analytical resources for analyzing the behavior of DR methods. The results indicate FADEx yields robust and reliable explanations, outperforming existing approaches in several aspects.

AI.tldr: FADEx is a novel local per-instance feature attribution method for explaining dimensionality reduction (DR) techniques. It uses first-order Taylor expansion and Singular Value Decomposition via weighted least squares to compute local linear approximations, making it agnostic to any DR method. FADEx provides both local feature attributions and distortion analysis without requiring out-of-sample data mapping, and outperforms existing DR explanation approaches in robustness and reliability.
AI.motivation: Non-linear DR techniques act as opaque transformations, making it difficult to understand how individual features influence instance positioning in the reduced space. Existing DR explanation approaches suffer from limitations such as multiple attributions per feature and restricted applicability to specific DR methods, hindering their practical use.
AI.method: FADEx computes local per-instance feature attributions by leveraging local linear approximation via first-order Taylor expansion and Singular Value Decomposition. It fits local linear models using weighted least squares, which eliminates the need for out-of-sample data mapping and makes the method agnostic to the underlying DR technique. The approach simultaneously provides local feature attributions and distortion analysis.
AI.result: Through qualitative and quantitative evaluations, comparisons with existing methods, and case studies, FADEx demonstrates effectiveness and versatility in explaining DR methods. The results show that FADEx yields robust and reliable explanations, outperforming existing approaches in several aspects.
AI.conclusion: FADEx provides a method-agnostic, robust approach to explaining dimensionality reduction results at the per-instance level, offering both feature attributions and distortion analysis as analytical resources for understanding DR behavior.

title: EgoGVAE: Ego-body Mesh Reconstruction via Guided Variational Autoencoder
summary: We address the problem of recovering the full-body mesh from only the head pose. This task has become essential for various applications based on head-mounted devices or smart glasses. The challenge of this task lies in estimating the pose information of unobserved body parts based solely on a single joint (i.e., head) trajectory. Several studies have begun to adopt head-conditioned generative models, however, such previous methods are costly and time-consuming due to the diffusion-based iterative process. As an alternative, we propose a simple yet novel method that leverages the latent space of the guidance network, which is designed as a variational autoencoder taking full-body poses as inputs. By enforcing latent distributions of this guidance network and our head-to-motion network to be similar, latent features sampled from the 'guided' distribution, i.e., distribution learned in our head-to-motion network, can be reliably decoded for natural representations of full-body poses even only with the head pose. One important advantage of the proposed method is that one-step sampling scheme achieves remarkably fast inference (more than 50 times faster) compared to diffusion-based approaches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the proposed method efficiently improves the performance of ego-body mesh reconstruction.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a non-diffusion method to recover full-body mesh from only head pose, using a VAE-based guidance network to align latent distributions, enabling fast one-step inference that is more than 50x faster than diffusion-based approaches while improving ego-body mesh reconstruction performance.
AI.motivation: Full-body mesh recovery from head pose is essential for head-mounted device and smart glasses applications, but existing head-conditioned diffusion-based generative methods are costly and time-consuming due to iterative sampling processes.
AI.method: The proposed method uses a variational autoencoder (VAE) guidance network that takes full-body poses as input. A head-to-motion network is trained so that its latent distribution matches the guidance network's latent distribution, allowing reliably decoded full-body poses from head pose only. A one-step sampling scheme enables fast inference.
AI.result: The method achieves more than 50 times faster inference than diffusion-based approaches and shows improved performance on benchmark datasets for ego-body mesh reconstruction.
AI.conclusion: Latent-distribution alignment between a guidance VAE and a head-to-motion network provides an efficient alternative to diffusion-based generative models for head-only full-body pose estimation, balancing quality and speed.

title: CORE: In-Context Reconstruction for Unified Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Tabular anomaly detection (TAD), which focuses on identifying abnormal samples that deviate from the majority in tabular data, has received growing attention. Recently, there has been an emerging trend towards unified TAD, which seeks to detect anomalies across different datasets using a single generalizable model. In unified TAD, aligning heterogeneous data remains challenging. While existing methods often rely on distance-based unified feature construction, they may obscure the semantics of the original features. Moreover, existing approaches typically formulate anomaly detection as a binary classification task, which may overlook diverse anomaly patterns from various datasets and be misled by unrepresentative synthetic anomalies. To address these challenges, we propose an in-COntext REconstruction approach for unified TAD (CORE for short). It introduces a decorrelated feature alignment module to directly align heterogeneous features into a unified representation space, which retains their semantic information. Meanwhile, CORE formulates unified TAD as an in-context reconstruction problem, eliminating the need for labeled or synthesized anomalies. Specifically, the in-context reconstruction module reconstructs each sample by leveraging contextual normal samples to capture dataset-specific distributions, such that reconstruction errors reflect its deviation from normality, facilitating unified TAD on arbitrary unseen datasets.

AI.tldr: CORE is an in-context reconstruction approach for unified tabular anomaly detection that uses a decorrelated feature alignment module to preserve semantic information across heterogeneous datasets and formulates anomaly detection as a reconstruction problem using contextual normal samples, eliminating the need for labeled or synthetic anomalies.
AI.motivation: Unified tabular anomaly detection faces two key challenges: (1) existing distance-based unified feature construction methods obscure the semantics of original features when aligning heterogeneous data, and (2) formulating anomaly detection as binary classification overlooks diverse anomaly patterns and can be misled by unrepresentative synthetic anomalies.
AI.method: CORE introduces a decorrelated feature alignment module to directly align heterogeneous features into a unified representation space while preserving semantic information, and formulates unified TAD as an in-context reconstruction problem. The in-context reconstruction module reconstructs each sample by leveraging contextual normal samples to capture dataset-specific distributions, using reconstruction errors to reflect deviation from normality.
AI.result: The approach eliminates the need for labeled or synthesized anomalies and enables unified anomaly detection on arbitrary unseen datasets by using reconstruction errors as the anomaly score.
AI.conclusion: CORE addresses the limitations of prior unified TAD methods by preserving feature semantics through decorrelated alignment and avoiding reliance on possibly misleading synthetic anomalies through an in-context reconstruction formulation that captures dataset-specific normal distributions.

title: Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring
summary: The information flow in the graph neural networks (GNNs) is fundamentally constrained by over-squashing, where structural bottlenecks impede long range information propagation. Graph-rewiring methods, which modify graph topology, have been extensively used to alleviate this. However, existing approaches often introduce prohibitive structural and computational bottlenecks, fail to preserve the critical properties of original graphs, and increase the edge counts massively. We introduce a novel method Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring , a group-theoretic rewiring method that augments the input graph with a Schreier-Coset graph derived from a special linear group. Our method provides theoretical guarantees, a graph that exhibits spectral gap and a bounded effective resistance, creating a low-resistance bypass for long-range communication. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that SCGR reduces effective resistance by 5-40% across various learning tasks, effectively mitigating connectivity bottlenecks while maintaining competitive accuracy.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring (SCGR), a group-theoretic method that augments input graphs with a Schreier-Coset graph derived from a special linear group to mitigate over-squashing in GNNs. The method provides theoretical guarantees including a spectral gap and bounded effective resistance, reducing effective resistance by 5-40% across learning tasks while maintaining competitive accuracy.
AI.motivation: Over-squashing in GNNs is fundamentally limited by structural bottlenecks that impede long-range information propagation. Existing graph-rewiring methods introduce prohibitive structural and computational bottlenecks, fail to preserve critical graph properties, and massively increase edge counts.
AI.method: The method augments the input graph with a Schreier-Coset graph derived from a special linear group, providing a group-theoretic rewiring approach that creates a low-resistance bypass for long-range communication, with theoretical guarantees of a spectral gap and bounded effective resistance.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations show SCGR reduces effective resistance by 5-40% across various learning tasks, effectively mitigating connectivity bottlenecks while maintaining competitive accuracy.
AI.conclusion: SCGR offers a theoretically grounded, group-theoretic solution to over-squashing that outperforms existing rewiring methods by providing spectral guarantees and bounded effective resistance while avoiding the structural/computational pitfalls of prior approaches.

title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmedical 2026: Architectural Diversity for Concept Detection and Foundation-Model Scaling for Caption Prediction in Medical Image Analysis
summary: We describe the DS@GT submissions to the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 challenge, which continues a long-running benchmark on the ROCOv2 dataset with two tracks: Concept Detection (Task 1), assigning UMLS Concept Unique Identifiers (CUIs) to radiology images, and Caption Prediction (Task 2), generating natural-language captions. For Task 1, our primary submission was a three-way late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16, and DenseNet-169 with a regularized ''Honest Threshold Tuning'' procedure designed to avoid validation overfitting on rare concepts; this submission ranked first on the official submission with a primary $F_1$ of $0.5790$ and a secondary $F_1$ of $0.9657$. In parallel, we submitted a training-free KNN retrieval pipeline over frozen BiomedCLIP embeddings, which reached a primary $F_1$ of $0.5780$ and a secondary $F_1$ of $0.9599$-essentially matching the fine-tuned ensemble on the primary track at a fraction of the cost. For Task 2, our submissions included a fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B model (overall $0.3571$, ranking third in the official submission), a fully fine-tuned BLIP pipeline with custom Vizwins merging ($0.3564$), and a zero-shot MedGemma-4B run with a PubMed-style prompt ($0.3186$), spanning a wide range of model scales and training costs. Code: https://github.com/dsgt-arc/imageclef-caption-2026.

AI.tldr: The DS@GT team's ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 submissions: a three-way late-fusion ensemble (ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP, DenseNet-169) with "Honest Threshold Tuning" that won Task 1 (concept detection) with primary F1 0.5790, a training-free KNN retrieval pipeline nearly matching it (0.5780), and multiple caption-generation systems for Task 2 led by a fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B (overall 0.3571, ranked third).
AI.motivation: To address the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 benchmark's two tracks—concept detection via UMLS CUIs and natural-language caption prediction—on the ROCOv2 dataset, exploring both fine-tuned ensembles and training-free retrieval approaches to balance accuracy against computational cost.
AI.method: Task 1 uses a three-way late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16, and DenseNet-169 with a "Honest Threshold Tuning" regularization procedure to avoid validation overfitting on rare concepts; a training-free KNN retrieval pipeline over frozen BiomedCLIP embeddings is also evaluated. Task 2 uses a fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B, a fully fine-tuned BLIP pipeline with custom Vizwins merging, and a zero-shot MedGemma-4B with PubMed-style prompting.
AI.result: Task 1 ensemble ranked first with primary F1 of 0.5790 and secondary F1 of 0.9657. The training-free KNN retrieval reached primary F1 0.5780 and secondary F1 0.9599, nearly matching the ensemble at much lower cost. Task 2 results: Gemma-3 27B overall 0.3571 (ranked third), BLIP with Vizwins merging 0.3564, zero-shot MedGemma-4B 0.3186.
AI.conclusion: A fine-tuned ensemble produces the top concept-detection result, but a training-free retrieval approach is nearly competitive at a fraction of cost, while Task 2 demonstrates a spectrum of caption-generation systems across model scales and training budgets.

title: Hidden APIs in Language Models: Discovering Reusable Causal Interfaces from Forked Futures
summary: Identical language-model answers can arise from hidden states that support different future computations, so current-answer probes do not establish a reusable internal interface. We introduce forked futures: future operations are sampled only after a prefix state has formed, and states are compared through the response distributions induced by those operations. This yields an empirical causal quotient over hidden states without requiring researcher-specified latent labels. Shared, Local, Mixture, and Distributed interfaces then compete under prequential causal description length subject to future-signature fidelity and matched capacity constraints. In the two detailed model evaluations, Shared has the lowest held-out description length, with gains of 0.216 nats on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 0.294 nats on Llama-3-8B, while maintaining tightly clustered mean future-signature distortion; a five-backbone sweep preserves the positive direction of Sharedness Gain. The figure-aligned transplantation analysis gives Shared the strongest joint target-correctness, locality, copy-preservation, and composite profile, and API-aligned paths mediate 0.749 of the target effect versus 0.150 for matched null paths. In the blind four-class model-organism test, 14/16 architectures are recovered, with one observed non-Shared to Shared error among 12 non-Shared organisms. These results support an economical reusable causal interface within the tested operation banks, while keeping the claim explicitly conditional on the candidate architectures, interventions, and held-out futures.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces "forked futures," a method to identify reusable internal causal interfaces in language models by sampling future operations after a prefix state forms and comparing induced response distributions. Under prequential causal description length with capacity matching, Shared interfaces achieve the lowest held-out description length (gains of 0.216 nats on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 0.294 nats on Llama-3-8B), strongest transplantation profiles, mediation of 0.749 of target effect, and 14/16 architecture recovery in a blind test—supporting an economical reusable causal interface conditional on tested architectures and operations.
AI.motivation: Identical language-model answers can arise from hidden states supporting different future computations, so current-answer probes fail to establish a reusable internal interface. The authors aim to move beyond label-based probing to an empirical, causal characterization of hidden states.
AI.method: Future operations are sampled after a prefix state forms; states are compared via induced response distributions ("forked futures"). This yields an empirical causal quotient over hidden states without researcher-specified latent labels. Shared, Local, Mixture, and Distributed interface hypotheses compete under prequential causal description length, subject to future-signature fidelity and matched capacity constraints. Analyses include two detailed model evaluations, a five-backbone sweep, figure-aligned transplantation, and a blind four-class model-organism test.
AI.result: Shared achieves the lowest held-out description length with gains of 0.216 nats (Qwen2.5-1.5B) and 0.294 nats (Llama-3-8B), while maintaining tightly clustered mean future-signature distortion. A five-backbone sweep preserves the positive direction of Sharedness Gain. Transplantation gives Shared the strongest joint profile (target-correctness, locality, copy-preservation, composite); API-aligned paths mediate 0.749 of target effect vs. 0.150 for null paths. In the blind test, 14/16 architectures are recovered, with one non-Shared to Shared error among 12 non-Shared organisms.
AI.conclusion: The results support an economical reusable causal interface within the tested operation banks, but the claim is explicitly conditional on the candidate architectures, interventions, and held-out futures considered.

title: HALO: Heterogeneous Admission through Localized Obligations for Safe Agentic Execution
summary: Recent agentic AI systems may return a heterogeneous response containing notices, requests, handoffs, and actions. Conditions can change before external use, so components from the same response need not remain supported together. Rejecting the whole response discards useful components, whereas checking components independently can leave a dependent without its prerequisite. We present Heterogeneous Admission with Localized Obligations (HALO), a runtime protocol that preserves supported components whose declared prerequisites also remain supported, rechecks each exact action before dispatch, and allows blocked actions to be replaced only by fresh candidates. HALO matched all 96 admission expectations and passed all 20 protocol tests. In structured-response replay, it retained 248/248 supported components, including 128/128 unaffected by unrelated changes, while a whole-response policy retained 0/248. Across ten cold-start PX4/Gazebo sessions, HALO blocked every tested stale route, observed no matching stale setpoint, and completed all fresh recoveries.

AI.tldr: HALO is a runtime protocol for agentic AI systems that selectively admits heterogeneous response components by preserving those whose declared prerequisites remain supported, rechecking each action before dispatch, and allowing blocked actions to be replaced only by fresh candidates. It passed 96 admission expectations and 20 protocol tests, retained all 248 supported components in replay (vs 0 for whole-response policy), and blocked all stale routes in PX4/Gazebo cold-start sessions.
AI.motivation: Agentic AI systems return heterogeneous responses (notices, requests, handoffs, actions). Conditions can change before external use, so components from the same response may no longer remain supported together. Rejecting the whole response discards useful components, while independent checking can leave a dependent without its prerequisite—motivating a finer-grained admission protocol.
AI.method: HALO presents a runtime protocol that preserves supported components whose declared prerequisites remain supported, rechecks each exact action before dispatch, and restricts blocked-action replacement to fresh candidates only.
AI.result: HALO matched all 96 admission expectations and passed all 20 protocol tests. In structured-response replay, it retained 248/248 supported components (including 128/128 unaffected by unrelated changes), versus 0/248 for a whole-response policy. In ten PX4/Gazebo cold-start sessions, HALO blocked every tested stale route, observed no matching stale setpoint, and completed all fresh recoveries.
AI.conclusion: Heterogeneous component-level admission, with prerequisite tracking and exact-action rechecking, substantially outperforms whole-response rejection by keeping useful components while guarding against stale or unsupported actions.

title: Latent States in Neural Networks: Recovering the Temporal Structure of Drifting Data from Model Weights
summary: A temporally drifting data stream may pass through discrete regimes rather than changing continuously. We ask whether such regimes are recoverable from the weights of models trained on the stream, using a hidden Markov model (HMM) fit to the chronologically ordered trajectory of those weights. We study this question in two domains known to drift over time: multimodal misinformation detection, using the Fakeddit dataset; and sentiment analysis, using the Yelp dataset. We train classifiers on consecutive temporal windows and fit an HMM to the trajectory of their aligned weights, recovering latent states that partition each timeline into coherent phases. On both datasets, classifiers generalize better to data from windows sharing the state of their training window than to windows across state boundaries. This within-state transfer advantage survives a control for temporal proximity and modestly exceeds the advantage recovered by a naive partition into contiguous states of equal size. Although the states are estimated solely from model weights, they correlate more strongly with shifts in the data's class distribution than with the weight-space geometry used to estimate them. After class divergence and lag are residualized out, the within-state advantage exceeds its permutation null on both tasks, indicating that the states recover structure relevant to transfer beyond the data distribution. Every effect replicates on both tasks but is attenuated on Yelp, whose label distribution is more temporally stable.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates whether discrete temporal regimes in drifting data streams can be recovered by fitting a hidden Markov model (HMM) to the trajectory of model weights trained on consecutive windows. On Fakeddit (misinformation) and Yelp (sentiment), recovered latent states partition timelines into coherent phases, yielding within-state transfer advantages that survive temporal-proximity and distribution controls.
AI.motivation: Temporally drifting data streams may transition through discrete regimes rather than evolving continuously. The authors ask whether these regimes can be recovered purely from model weights, which would provide a lightweight signal for detecting phase transitions without relying on data labels or distribution statistics.
AI.method: Classifiers are trained on consecutive temporal windows; their aligned weights form a trajectory over time. An HMM is fit to this chronological weight trajectory, recovering latent states that segment the timeline into phases. Transfer performance within states is compared to across states, with controls for temporal proximity, equal-size contiguous partitions, class-distribution shifts, and permutation nulls.
AI.result: On both datasets, classifiers generalize better within the same HMM state than across state boundaries, an advantage that persists after controlling for temporal proximity and exceeds naive contiguous partitions. States correlate more strongly with class-distribution shifts than with weight-space geometry, and the within-state advantage survives residualization of class divergence and permutation tests on both tasks, though the effect is attenuated on Yelp where the label distribution is more temporally stable.
AI.conclusion: Discrete regimes in drifting streams are recoverable from model-weight trajectories via HMM, and these states capture transfer-relevant structure that goes beyond both temporal proximity and raw class-distribution shifts. The approach yields consistent but task-dependent evidence, with stronger effects when label distributions drift more.

title: Private Face Recognition Training Dataset Publication via Identity-Decoupled and Geometry-Preserving Face Distillation
summary: Publishing private face recognition~(FR) training datasets is privacy-sensitive because faces expose identity information. Private FR training dataset publication mitigates this risk by releasing protected proxies as substitutes for private training faces. However, training FR models with such data introduces an identity paradox: \emph{the identity cues that make released faces useful for recognition supervision are also the cues that make them linkable to real individuals.} A protected face should be decoupled from the original identity, yet still behave as a reliable identity sample for training. Removing these cues too aggressively may destroy the class structure needed for recognition learning, whereas preserving them too faithfully may increase source-identity linkability. We argue that this paradox stems from conflating source-aligned identity semantics with recognition-useful proxy identity geometry. The former should be suppressed to reduce linkage to private individuals, while the latter should be preserved for FR learning. Based on this insight, we propose \textbf{Private Face Distillation}, an identity-decoupling and geometry-preserving framework. It uses Orthogonal Geometry Preservation to construct decoupled proxy identities from private identity representations while maintaining hyperspherical geometry, and Relational Topology Alignment to preserve identity relations for recognition learning. Experiments across multiple domain-shifted FR scenarios show that Private Face Distillation achieves stronger utility than the evaluated publication baselines. On IJB-C surveillance, it improves $\mathrm{TAR}@\mathrm{FAR}{=}1\text{e-}{3}$ by 3.94\% over the baseline while reducing source-identity linkability. These results suggest that private FR training dataset publication should decouple source-identity correspondence while preserving proxy identity geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Private Face Distillation, a framework for publishing private face recognition training datasets that decouples source-identity semantics while preserving recognition-useful proxy identity geometry, achieving stronger utility and reduced linkability.
AI.motivation: Publishing private face recognition training datasets is privacy-sensitive due to identity exposure. There is an identity paradox: identity cues needed for recognition supervision are the same cues that make faces linkable to real individuals. Existing approaches either destroy class structure needed for recognition learning or preserve cues too faithfully, increasing source-identity linkability.
AI.method: Private Face Distillation is an identity-decoupling and geometry-preserving framework with two key components: (1) Orthogonal Geometry Preservation constructs decoupled proxy identities from private identity representations while maintaining hyperspherical geometry, and (2) Relational Topology Alignment preserves identity relations for recognition learning.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple domain-shifted FR scenarios show stronger utility than evaluated publication baselines. On IJB-C surveillance, it improves TAR@FAR=1e-3 by 3.94% over the baseline while reducing source-identity linkability.
AI.conclusion: Private FR training dataset publication should decouple source-identity correspondence while preserving proxy identity geometry, resolving the identity paradox by separating source-aligned identity semantics from recognition-useful proxy identity geometry.

title: SCOPE: Synthetic Conditional Objectives for Policy Evolution in Black-Box Combinatorial Optimization
comment: 43 pages; Kiet, Duc, and Bang contributed equally
summary: Black-box combinatorial optimization requires systematically identifying high-quality solutions under a limited evaluation budget, yet the unknown objective function provides little guidance for deciding where the search should explore next. We introduce SCOPE, a general framework for Synthetic Conditional Objectives for Policy Evolution in Black-Box Combinatorial Optimization. Rather than directly optimizing the inaccessible objective, SCOPE learns a set of synthetic objectives conditioned on the accumulated search history, where each objective is designed to expose a distinct and potentially useful preference over candidate solutions. These objectives are then used to evolve search policies that generate diverse candidates, whose true quality is subsequently assessed through black-box evaluations. The outer loop adaptively updates and selects synthetic objectives according to how effectively their induced policies discover promising regions. In contrast, the inner loop returns a portfolio of top-performing policies to reduce the risk of relying on a single surrogate preference. This formulation reframes objective design as a mechanism for guiding policy exploration, enabling the search process to exploit observed evidence while maintaining structured diversity across discrete solution spaces. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark problems demonstrate that SCOPE consistently improves black-box search performance under limited evaluation budgets and generalizes well across diverse combinatorial structures.

AI.tldr: SCOPE is a framework for black-box combinatorial optimization that learns synthetic objective functions conditioned on search history to evolve diverse search policies, with an outer loop adapting objectives and an inner loop returning a portfolio of top policies, consistently outperforming baselines under limited evaluation budgets.
AI.motivation: Black-box combinatorial optimization struggles with limited evaluation budgets and an inaccessible objective function that offers little guidance on where to search next. Direct optimization of the unknown objective is infeasible, motivating a framework that uses learned synthetic objectives to guide policy exploration.
AI.method: SCOPE learns synthetic objectives conditioned on accumulated search history, each exposing a distinct preference over candidate solutions. These objectives evolve search policies that generate diverse candidates, which are evaluated via black-box evaluations. An outer loop adaptively updates and selects objectives based on how effectively their induced policies discover promising regions, while an inner loop maintains a portfolio of top-performing policies to mitigate reliance on a single surrogate preference.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark problems show SCOPE consistently improves black-box search performance under limited evaluation budgets and generalizes well across diverse combinatorial structures.
AI.conclusion: SCOPE reframes objective design as a mechanism for guiding policy exploration, enabling search to exploit observed evidence while maintaining structured diversity across discrete solution spaces, offering a general and effective solution for black-box combinatorial optimization with constrained budgets.

title: Old Tricks, New Models: How Simple Image Transformations Break Modern AI-based Content Moderation
summary: While automated content-moderation systems have become essential for screening harmful content at scale, conventional task-specific classifiers often provide limited policy cov- erage and contextual understanding. Recently, commercial multimodal moderation APIs built on large foundation models have been introduced with the promise of providing broader and more capable safety filters. In this work, we analyze whether this shift also yields more robust image moderation. We conduct a large-scale black-box evaluation on three established commercial image-moderation services and compare their robustness. By evaluating seven simple, model-agnostic image transformations across multiple providers, datasets, harm categories, perceptual-similarity constraints, and transformation intensities, we find that: (1) all three commercial services can be bypassed using inexpensive image transformations that require no gradients, surrogate models, or knowledge of the target system; (2) even fixed transformations such as color inversion and grayscale conversion induce unsafe-to-safe decision changes while preserving content that remains recognizable to humans; (3) their robustness varies substantially across datasets and harm categories, with multimodal content and self-harm exhibiting pronounced vulnerabilities. This yields the conclusion that replacing conventional moderation classifiers with foundation-model-based APIs does not, by itself, provide a reliable security boundary. Such systems must be evaluated under realistic transformations and deployed as one component of a layered moderation pipeline rather than as standalone safety filters.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts a large-scale black-box robustness evaluation of three commercial multimodal moderation APIs, finding that all can be bypassed by simple, gradient-free image transformations like color inversion and grayscale conversion—especially for multimodal content and self-harm categories—concluding that foundation-model-based moderation APIs do not provide a reliable security boundary and should be deployed as part of layered moderation pipelines.
AI.motivation: Conventional task-specific content-moderation classifiers offer limited policy coverage and contextual understanding, while commercial multimodal moderation APIs built on large foundation models promise broader and more capable safety filters. The authors question whether this shift also yields more robust image moderation, motivating a systematic robustness comparison across commercial services.
AI.method: The authors conduct a large-scale black-box evaluation of three established commercial image-moderation services. They apply seven simple, model-agnostic image transformations across multiple providers, datasets, harm categories, perceptual-similarity constraints, and transformation intensities, requiring no gradients, surrogate models, or knowledge of the target system.
AI.result: Three key findings: (1) all three commercial services can be bypassed using inexpensive image transformations requiring no gradients or surrogate models; (2) even fixed transformations such as color inversion and grayscale conversion induce unsafe-to-safe decision changes while content remains human-recognizable; (3) robustness varies substantially across datasets and harm categories, with multimodal content and self-harm showing pronounced vulnerabilities.
AI.conclusion: Replacing conventional moderation classifiers with foundation-model-based APIs does not by itself provide a reliable security boundary. Such systems must be evaluated under realistic transformations and deployed as one component of a layered moderation pipeline rather than as standalone safety filters.

title: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Collider Physics with Multi-Domain Adaptation
summary: We present a lightweight approach to foundation modeling (\textbf{NEXUS}) that leverages pre-trained learning from collider physics data towards out-of-domain tasks in other scientific datasets, using a fully connected autoencoder model with approximately 3 million parameters. The model pre-trains with no supervision over a large-scale collision dataset from the Large Hadron Collider modeled by charged particle track features. Downstream tasks for collider analyses, such as kinematic regression and event classification, are developed on pre-trained model weights and achieve improved accuracy with only small labeled datasets when compared to equivalent architectures trained from scratch. The benefits of pre-training are additionally investigated through latent space interpretation and application to other domains, including gravitational waves, flood forecasting, and neural activity. Furthermore, the relative computational simplicity of NEXUS is demonstrated compared to transformer approaches at comparable scale, opening the door to power-efficient inference and real-time or edge applications of foundation models in scientific experiments.

AI.tldr: NEXUS is a lightweight (~3M parameter) fully connected autoencoder foundation model pre-trained on Large Hadron Collider charged particle track data, demonstrating transfer learning to out-of-domain scientific tasks (gravitational waves, flood forecasting, neural activity) with improved accuracy on small labeled datasets and computational efficiency compared to transformer-based approaches.
AI.motivation: Foundation models in scientific domains typically rely on large transformer architectures that are computationally expensive, limiting their deployment in power-constrained settings such as real-time or edge applications. The authors aim to show that a lightweight, fully connected autoencoder can serve as an effective and efficient foundation model for physics data, while also demonstrating transferability to other scientific domains outside high-energy physics.
AI.method: NEXUS uses a fully connected autoencoder with approximately 3 million parameters, pre-trained without supervision on large-scale LHC collision data encoded via charged particle track features. Downstream tasks (kinematic regression and event classification) are built on pre-trained weights and fine-tuned with small labeled datasets. The study also examines latent space interpretability and applies the pre-trained model to gravitational wave, flood forecasting, and neural activity datasets, benchmarking computational cost against transformer models of comparable scale.
AI.result: Pre-trained downstream models achieve improved accuracy with small labeled datasets compared to equivalent architectures trained from scratch. The model shows successful transfer to out-of-domain scientific tasks including gravitational waves, flood forecasting, and neural activity. NEXUS demonstrates significantly lower computational requirements than transformer approaches at comparable scale, enabling power-efficient and real-time/edge deployment.
AI.conclusion: A lightweight autoencoder-based foundation model can effectively capture generalizable representations from collider physics data and transfer them to diverse scientific domains, offering a computationally practical alternative to transformer-based foundation models for scientific applications, particularly where power efficiency and real-time inference are critical.

title: CXR-Retrieve: Compositional Text-to-Image Retrieval in Chest Radiography
summary:
Large chest radiography archives are difficult to search because most studies are paired only with free-text reports rather than structured clinical annotations. Vision-language models offer a natural interface for text-to-image retrieval, but current biomedical models are primarily optimized for report-to-image matching rather than for satisfying short clinical search queries. This creates an objective mismatch: a model may retrieve images related to words in the query while failing to satisfy the full clinical constraint, especially for conjunctions and negations such as ``atelectasis and no pneumonia.''
  We introduce CXR-Retrieve, a structured benchmark for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval. The benchmark contains 5,159 test images from the official test-split of MIMIC-CXR-JPG and 145 textual queries spanning single and conjunction findings, both positive and negative. Relevance is defined by whether a retrieved image satisfies all asserted pathology constraints, rather than by whether it matches a paired report.
  We further propose a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective for clinical retrieval. Our method attracts image-text pairs with compatible asserted pathology constraints, including shared confirmed absences, while explicitly repelling contradictory pairs. Starting from the in-domain CXR-CLIP checkpoint, our method improves Precision@5 over CXR-CLIP by 8.5 percentage points on two-pathology conjunctions and by 22.0 percentage points on negation queries. These results show that reliable chest X-ray retrieval requires training objectives that model not only which findings are mentioned, but also how they are clinically asserted.

AI.tldr: CXR-Retrieve is a structured benchmark for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval, addressing the mismatch between report-to-image matching and short clinical query satisfaction. It introduces a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective that models asserted pathology constraints (including negations and conjunctions), improving Precision@5 by up to 22 percentage points over CXR-CLIP on negation queries.
AI.motivation: Large chest radiography archives are hard to search because they lack structured annotations. Vision-language models provide text-to-image retrieval, but current biomedical models are optimized for report-to-image matching rather than short clinical queries. This creates an objective mismatch: models may retrieve images matching query keywords while failing the complete clinical constraint, particularly for conjunctions and negations (e.g., "atelectasis and no pneumonia").
AI.method: The authors introduce CXR-Retrieve, a benchmark with 5,159 test images from MIMIC-CXR-JPG and 145 textual queries spanning single/conjunction findings with positive/negative assertions. Relevance is defined by whether images satisfy all asserted pathology constraints. They propose a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective that attracts image-text pairs with compatible asserted pathology constraints (including shared confirmed absences) and repels contradictory pairs, starting from the in-domain CXR-CLIP checkpoint.
AI.result: The proposed method improves Precision@5 over CXR-CLIP by 8.5 percentage points on two-pathology conjunctions and by 22.0 percentage points on negation queries.
AI.conclusion: Reliable chest X-ray retrieval requires training objectives that model not only which findings are mentioned but also how they are clinically asserted (e.g., presence vs. absence), demonstrating that compositional understanding is essential for clinically meaningful retrieval.

title: ReDiPPO: Reference-Guided Value Calibration and Discrepancy-Aware Token Reweighting for Mathematical Reasoning
summary: Reinforcement learning has emerged as an effective paradigm for enhancing the mathematical reasoning capabilities of large language models. Among existing policy optimization methods, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) remains particularly appealing because its learned critic can, in principle, provide token-level credit assignment. However, in mathematical reasoning tasks characterized by long reasoning horizons and sparse outcome rewards, reliable token-level credit assignment remains challenging. The standard critic often fails to accurately evaluate intermediate reasoning states, resulting in noisy advantage estimates and suboptimal policy updates. In this paper, we propose ReDiPPO, a Reference-guided and Discrepancy-aware PPO framework for mathematical reasoning. ReDiPPO introduces a reference-guided critic that uses reference answers as training-time privileged signals to provide more accurate value estimation. Meanwhile, it retains a standard critic and quantifies the token-level reference-standard discrepancy between the standard value estimate and the reference-guided value estimate. This discrepancy serves as an indicator of difficult reasoning states and is used to reweight the corresponding token-level advantages during PPO optimization. Extensive experiments on diverse mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that ReDiPPO improves value-estimation accuracy and consistently outperforms strong policy optimization baselines, including PPO, DAPO, and GSPO, in final reasoning performance. Our code is available on https://github.com/cii030/ReDiPPO.

AI.tldr: ReDiPPO is a Reference-guided and Discrepancy-aware PPO framework that improves token-level credit assignment in mathematical reasoning by using reference answers as privileged signals to guide the critic and reweighting token-level advantages based on reference-standard discrepancy.
AI.motivation: PPO with a learned critic is appealing for mathematical reasoning due to potential token-level credit assignment, but in long-horizon reasoning tasks with sparse rewards, the standard critic produces noisy advantage estimates and suboptimal policy updates.
AI.method: ReDiPPO introduces a reference-guided critic that uses reference answers as training-time privileged signals for more accurate value estimation, while retaining a standard critic. It computes a token-level reference-standard discrepancy between the two critics' value estimates, which serves as an indicator of difficult reasoning states and is used to reweight corresponding token-level advantages during PPO optimization.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on diverse mathematical reasoning benchmarks show ReDiPPO improves value-estimation accuracy and consistently outperforms strong baselines including PPO, DAPO, and GSPO in final reasoning performance.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging reference-guided privileged signals and discrepancy-aware advantage reweighting enhances token-level credit assignment and overall mathematical reasoning performance in policy optimization.

title: Sparsity Induced Identifiability in Matrix Tri-Factorisation
summary: Matrix factorisation is a fundamental tool for exploiting low-dimensional structure in high-dimensional data, with applications such as data compression, denoising, structure discovery, interpretable representation learning, and dimensionality reduction. Compared to conventional two-factor models, matrix tri-factorisation provides greater modelling flexibility, while sparsity constraints often improve both interpretability and recovery performance. Although the role of sparsity has been extensively studied for two-factor matrix factorisation, rigorous theoretical guarantees for general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation remain largely unexplored. To address this gap, we establish, to the best of our knowledge, the first rigorous theoretical study for sparsity-induced identifiability in general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation. Our analysis is enabled by a novel decomposition strategy that transforms the original problem into two coupled auxiliary factorisation problems, while preserving the structural information necessary to the recovery of the original factor matrices from the observations. Building upon this decomposition, we derive recovery guarantees and structural consistency results that characterise how coefficient sparsity influences the sufficient recovery conditions, convergence behaviour, spectral approximation error, high-probability bounds, and structure preservation. Comprehensive Monte Carlo experiments validate the proposed theory and demonstrate close agreement between the theoretical results and empirical observations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first rigorous theoretical study of sparsity-induced identifiability in general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation, enabled by a novel decomposition strategy that transforms the original problem into two coupled auxiliary factorisation problems, with recovery guarantees and structural consistency results validated by Monte Carlo experiments.
AI.motivation: Matrix tri-factorisation offers greater modelling flexibility than two-factor models and sparsity constraints improve interpretability and recovery, yet rigorous theoretical guarantees for general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation have been largely unexplored despite extensive study of sparsity in two-factor factorisation.
AI.method: A novel decomposition strategy transforms the matrix tri-factorisation problem into two coupled auxiliary factorisation problems while preserving structural information needed for recovery of original factor matrices, enabling derivation of recovery guarantees and structural consistency results.
AI.result: Recovery guarantees and structural consistency results characterise how coefficient sparsity influences sufficient recovery conditions, convergence behaviour, spectral approximation error, high-probability bounds, and structure preservation. Comprehensive Monte Carlo experiments validate the theory with close agreement to empirical observations.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes the first rigorous theoretical framework for sparsity-induced identifiability in general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation, providing both theoretical guarantees and empirical validation.

title: FDDWAN: A Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Network for Watermarking Attack
summary: Existing invisible watermark removal methods often struggle to accurately capture the watermark-bearing features, leading to an unfavorable trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity. In this paper, we propose the Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Watermark Attack Network (FDDWAN), a coarse-to-fine framework that performs watermark removal through wavelet-domain decomposition and residual diffusion refinement. In the initial stage, the Wavelet-based Frequency-domain Preliminary Attack Module (WFPAM) decomposes the watermarked image into low- and high-frequency subbands and applies frequency-specific attack strategies tailored to their respective contributions to watermark robustness and perceptual quality. In the next stage, the Frequency-domain Residual Diffusion Attack Module (FRDAM) separately models the residual distributions between the preliminarily attacked outputs and the corresponding watermark-free references during training. Rather than reconstructing the entire image, FRDAM selectively refines frequency-domain residuals, directing the diffusion process toward the remaining watermark related discrepancies while minimizing modifications to image content. Extensive experiments on CelebA and ImageNet across four representative watermarking schemes demonstrate that FDDWAN achieves a more favorable trade-off between watermark removal effectiveness and visual fidelity than conventional and learning-based attack methods.

AI.tldr: FDDWAN is a coarse-to-fine diffusion-based watermark removal network that decomposes watermarked images in the wavelet domain and uses frequency-decoupled residual diffusion refinement to achieve a better trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity.
AI.motivation: Existing invisible watermark removal methods struggle to accurately capture watermark-bearing features, resulting in an unfavorable trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity.
AI.method: The framework has two stages: (1) WFPAM decomposes the watermarked image into low- and high-frequency subbands via wavelet transform and applies frequency-specific attack strategies; (2) FRDAM models residual distributions between preliminary attacked outputs and watermark-free references during training, selectively refining frequency-domain residuals to direct diffusion toward remaining watermark discrepancies while minimizing content modification.
AI.result: Experiments on CelebA and ImageNet across four watermarking schemes show FDDWAN achieves a more favorable trade-off between watermark removal effectiveness and visual fidelity than conventional and learning-based attack methods.
AI.conclusion: The frequency-decoupled coarse-to-fine diffusion approach provides a superior balance between removing invisible watermarks and preserving perceptual image quality, outperforming existing attack methods.

title: HealthCAT: An Interpretable Encoder-only Transformer Framework for Health Indicator Prediction and Temporal Interpretation of Wearable Sensor Data
summary: Wearable sensors continuously capture fine-grained multivariate time-series data, providing opportunities to model behavioural patterns associated with health outcomes. However, existing deep learning methods prioritise predictive accuracy over interpretability, limiting their application in health research. In this study, we present HealthCAT, a flexible framework that integrates an Encoder-only Transformer with an Attentive Class Activation Token (AttentiveCAT) to generate class-specific, time-step-level interpretations. These interpretations can be mapped back onto behavioural cycles that are relevant to the domain (e.g., time-of-day), supporting individual-level analysis of wearable sensor data. We evaluated HealthCAT using two real-world wearable sensor datasets (306 participants in total). HealthCAT outperformed deep learning baselines by up to 17\% in F1-score and 12\% in accuracy on both datasets ($p<0.05$). In masking experiments, the time steps identified by HealthCAT carried significantly more predictive value than random selection across all masking conditions ($p<0.05$), indicating that the identified time steps are predictively informative. By coupling predictive performance with validated time-step-level interpretability, HealthCAT moves wearable sensor analysis beyond aggregated metrics towards temporal patterns that support health monitoring, behavioural pattern analysis, and intervention design in health research. The significance of this work is that it enables accurate prediction of health indicators from wearable sensor data while providing insights into when and how physical activity patterns occur, rather than relying solely on aggregated summary measures.

AI.tldr: HealthCAT is a framework combining an Encoder-only Transformer with an Attentive Class Activation Token to provide accurate predictions on wearable sensor time-series data while generating class-specific, time-step-level interpretability. It outperforms deep learning baselines by up to 17% in F1-score and 12% in accuracy on two real-world datasets (306 participants), and masking experiments confirm the identified time steps carry significant predictive value.
AI.motivation: Existing deep learning methods for wearable sensor multivariate time-series data prioritize predictive accuracy over interpretability, limiting their application in health research where understanding behavioral patterns is crucial. There is a need for methods that not only predict health outcomes accurately but also provide meaningful temporal interpretations.
AI.method: HealthCAT integrates an Encoder-only Transformer with an Attentive Class Activation Token (AttentiveCAT). The framework generates class-specific, time-step-level interpretations that can be mapped back onto domain-relevant behavioural cycles (e.g., time-of-day), enabling individual-level analysis of wearable sensor data.
AI.result: HealthCAT outperformed deep learning baselines by up to 17% in F1-score and 12% in accuracy on both real-world wearable sensor datasets (p<0.05). Masking experiments showed that time steps identified by HealthCAT carried significantly more predictive value than random selection across all masking conditions (p<0.05).
AI.conclusion: HealthCAT moves wearable sensor analysis beyond aggregated metrics by coupling predictive performance with validated time-step-level interpretability, enabling accurate health indicator prediction while providing insights into when and how physical activity patterns occur—supporting health monitoring, behavioural pattern analysis, and intervention design.

title: Expanding Data-Agnostic Pivotal Instances Selection Models with Proximity Trees and Ensemble Learning
summary: As decision-making processes grow more complex, machine learning tools have become essential for tackling business and societal challenges. However, many existing methods rely on decision-making procedures that are difficult to interpret. Since humans naturally make decisions by comparing new cases with a few representative examples, we aim to design an approach that selects such pivots to construct an interpretable predictive model. Inspired by decision trees, we propose a hierarchical, interpretable-by-design pivot selection model based on the similarity between pivots and input instances. Our method functions both as a pivot selection technique and a standalone predictive model. Extending beyond single pivots, we incorporate pairs of pivots that are used by proximity and oblique trees, as well as ensembles, which enhance the versatility and effectiveness of our proposal. Additionally, our approach is data modality-agnostic, leveraging pre-trained networks for data transformation. Experiments across diverse datasets, including tabular data, text, images, and time series, demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming alternative instance selection strategies and achieving competitive results against state-of-the-art interpretable models while maintaining a minimal number of pivots.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a hierarchical, interpretable-by-design pivot selection model for machine learning that constructs predictive models using a small set of representative examples (pivots) chosen based on similarity to input instances. The method supports single and paired pivots (inspired by proximity and oblique trees), ensembles, and is modality-agnostic via pre-trained networks. Experiments across tabular, text, image, and time-series data show it outperforms alternative instance selection strategies and is competitive with state-of-the-art interpretable models while using minimal pivots.
AI.motivation: Many existing machine learning methods for complex decision-making are difficult to interpret. Since humans naturally make decisions by comparing new cases to a few representative examples, the authors aim to design an interpretable approach that selects such pivots to build a transparent predictive model.
AI.method: The method is a hierarchical, interpretable-by-design pivot selection model inspired by decision trees. It selects pivots based on similarity between pivots and input instances, functioning both as a pivot selection technique and a standalone predictive model. It extends to pairs of pivots (inspired by proximity and oblique trees) and ensembles. It is modality-agnostic, using pre-trained networks for data transformation.
AI.result: Experiments across tabular data, text, images, and time series show the approach outperforms alternative instance selection strategies and achieves competitive results against state-of-the-art interpretable models while maintaining a minimal number of pivots.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hierarchical pivot selection model provides an effective, interpretable approach to prediction across multiple data modalities, offering a balance between interpretability and predictive performance through minimal representative examples.

title: LoMeVQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Longitudinal Medical VQA
comment: 23 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/pepperbubble/LoMeVQA
summary: In clinical practice, patients often undergo multiple imaging examinations over successive visits, yielding longitudinal data. Modeling such temporal information is crucial for reliable assessment of disease progression and treatment response. However, despite the rapid advancement of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), longitudinal medical visual reasoning remains largely underexplored. To fill this gap, we propose LoMeVQA, a comprehensive benchmark consisting of 206K longitudinal visual question answering (VQA) pairs for temporal medical image analysis. LoMeVQA covers five tasks: progress classification, progress description, progress report generation, differential region grounding, and differential region description. To construct the dataset, we develop an automated pipeline that (1) organizes patient records chronologically, (2) extracts clinically meaningful entities via a medical knowledge graph, and (3) models their temporal evolution to guide large language models in generating high-quality longitudinal VQA pairs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that both general-purpose and medical-domain MLLMs perform poorly on LoMeVQA, revealing substantial limitations in temporal reasoning. To address these limitations, we introduce MedLong-8B, which achieves state-of-the-art performance across all tasks. Beyond benchmarking, we conduct detailed analyses that uncover key failure modes and shed light on how to improve longitudinal medical visual reasoning. Our data is available at: https://github.com/pepperbubble/LoMeVQA

AI.tldr: This paper introduces LoMeVQA, a large-scale benchmark (206K VQA pairs) for longitudinal medical visual reasoning, along with MedLong-8B, a model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on five temporal medical image analysis tasks. The work reveals that existing MLLMs struggle substantially with temporal reasoning in medical imaging.
AI.motivation: Patients commonly undergo multiple imaging exams over successive visits, producing longitudinal data essential for assessing disease progression and treatment response. Despite advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), longitudinal medical visual reasoning remains largely unexplored, creating a need for a dedicated benchmark and model.
AI.method: The authors propose LoMeVQA, a benchmark with 206K longitudinal VQA pairs covering five tasks: progress classification, progress description, progress report generation, differential region grounding, and differential region description.
