AI.conclusion: Qwen-UI-Agent demonstrates that a real-world-centric design—combining real-device runtime, unified GUI+CLI action space, data flywheel, and large-scale online RL—yields state-of-the-art mobile performance and competitive cross-platform results, supporting the viability of general-purpose GUI agents for real-world deployment.

title: From Expert Reduction to Behavioral Divergence: Tracing Numerical State through Sparse MoE Inference
summary: Mathematically equivalent expert-reduction orders can produce observably different sparse-MoE executions. We isolate this effect in native DeepSeek-V4-Flash by freezing local MoE state and varying only aggregation semantics. Four schemes separate operand representation from accumulator precision. At one layer-5 fork, 720 A-mode orders yield 10 continuation basins; 720 B-mode orders form 360 exact structural classes and 11 basins. Under one Chinese prompt, the B classes split into 202 layoffs, 113 hiring, and 45 other continuations. Maximum-L-infinity B-branch selection separates 12, 24, and 36 of 50 prompts by 8, 16, and 32 tokens. Across 192 persistent trajectories per scheme, P32, A, and B change every native-reference route trajectory, while C preserves routes, token sequences, and texts. A separate 192-trajectory C check matches native MoE, post-mHC, next-router, and LM states bitwise. For one controlled B branch, exact post-mHC endpoint reconstruction reproduces the measured downstream trajectory. At the next decode boundary, exact FP64 reconstruction of the branch's full persistent state yields agreement for 301 downstream post-mHC states, 301 persistent-state checkpoints, 301 routes, predictions, and text over seven steps, given the same naturally generated next input. These controls identify post-mHC as an intra-token boundary and full persistent state as a cross-token continuation boundary. Identical tokens need not imply identical autoregressive state: divergence can survive a token boundary and become visible later. These results make expert operand conversion, accumulator precision, and reduction order part of a numerical compatibility contract for sparse-MoE runtimes and hardware backends. They establish controlled causal possibility, not deployment incidence; C's order invariance is limited to evaluated six-term states and schedules.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that mathematically equivalent expert-reduction orders produce observably different sparse-MoE executions in DeepSeek-V4-Flash. By isolating aggregation semantics while freezing local MoE state, the authors show that different reduction schemes alter continuation basins, structural classes, model trajectories, and text outputs. They identify post-mHC as an intra-token boundary and full persistent state as a cross-token continuation boundary, showing that identical tokens need not imply identical autoregressive state. The work establishes expert operand conversion, accumulator precision, and reduction order as part of a numerical compatibility contract for sparse-MoE systems.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to investigate whether mathematically equivalent expert-reduction orders in sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can produce observably different execution outcomes due to numerical non-associativity. The authors aim to isolate and characterize this effect, and to identify precise boundaries (intra-token vs. cross-token) at which state divergence can propagate through autoregressive generation.
AI.method: The authors freeze local MoE state in native DeepSeek-V4-Flash and vary only aggregation semantics across four schemes that separate operand representation from accumulator precision. They compare A-mode and B-mode reduction orders at a layer-5 fork (720 orders each), analyze continuation basins and structural classes, and perform controlled reconstruction experiments: exact post-mHC endpoint reconstruction and exact FP64 reconstruction of full persistent state. They also run 192 persistent trajectories per scheme, tracking route trajectories, token sequences, texts, router states, and LM states, with bitwise comparison against native MoE behavior.
AI.result: At one layer-5 fork, 720 A-mode orders yield 10 continuation basins, while 720 B-mode orders form 360 exact structural classes and 11 basins. Under one Chinese prompt, B classes split into 202 layoffs, 113 hiring, and 45 other continuations. Maximum-L-infinity B-branch selection separates 12, 24, and 36 of 50 prompts by 8, 16, and 32 tokens. Across 192 trajectories, P32, A, and B change every native-reference route trajectory, while C preserves routes, token sequences, and texts bitwise. A separate 192-trajectory C check matches native MoE, post-mHC, next-router, and LM states bitwise. Exact post-mHC and FP64 persistent-state reconstructions reproduce measured downstream trajectories, yielding agreement across 301 states, checkpoints, routes, predictions, and text over seven steps.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that reduction order, operand conversion, and accumulator precision constitute a numerical compatibility contract for sparse-MoE runtimes and hardware backends. They establish controlled causal possibility (not deployment incidence): divergence can survive token boundaries and become visible later, meaning identical tokens need not imply identical autoregressive state. C's order invariance is limited to the evaluated six-term states and schedules.

title: ViewMind3D: Modular View-Aware Inference for Training-Free 3D-QA
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) have enabled new possibilities for 3D question answering (3D-QA), a key capability for embodied AI and robotic perception. However, most existing methods rely on 3D-specific training or fine-tuning with costly annotations, limiting their scalability and real-world applicability. We present \textbf{ViewMind3D}, a fully training-free and modular framework for 3D spatial reasoning over multi-view observations of a scene without requiring complete 3D reconstruction. The framework decomposes the 3D-QA task into four interpretable components: (1) question-driven multi-view selection, (2) guided visual grounding with language-conditioned object cues, (3) spatial context encoding via a bird's-eye-view (BEV) viewpoint indicator, and (4) structured answer generation through role-based reasoning. This design enables structured, robust, and interpretable reasoning without requiring model tuning. Experimental results on ScanQA and SQA3D show that ViewMind3D achieves competitive performance compared to prior training-free and fine-tuned 3D-LLMs. In particular, our method improves performance on spatially grounded question types, such as ``What'' questions in SQA3D, while maintaining strong overall accuracy (50.8\%) and achieving 73.4 CIDEr on ScanQA. These results demonstrate that effective 3D reasoning can be achieved through modular orchestration of general-purpose LLMs and VLMs for robotic perception in real-world environments.

AI.tldr: ViewMind3D is a training-free, modular framework for 3D question answering that decomposes the task into four interpretable components—multi-view selection, visual grounding, BEV-based spatial encoding, and role-based answer generation—achieving competitive performance on ScanQA (73.4 CIDEr) and SQA3D (50.8% accuracy) without any model fine-tuning or 3D reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D-QA methods require costly 3D-specific training or fine-tuning with expensive annotations, limiting scalability and real-world applicability. The authors aim to enable effective 3D spatial reasoning using general-purpose LLMs and VLMs without any training or complete 3D reconstruction.
AI.method: ViewMind3D decomposes 3D-QA into four interpretable modules: (1) question-driven multi-view selection, (2) guided visual grounding using language-conditioned object cues, (3) spatial context encoding via a bird's-eye-view (BEV) viewpoint indicator, and (4) structured answer generation through role-based reasoning. The framework orchestrates general-purpose LLMs and VLMs in a modular, training-free pipeline.
AI.result: On ScanQA, ViewMind3D achieves 73.4 CIDEr. On SQA3D, it achieves 50.8% overall accuracy, with notable improvements on spatially grounded "What" question types. It performs competitively against both prior training-free methods and fine-tuned 3D-LLMs.
AI.conclusion: Effective 3D spatial reasoning can be achieved through modular orchestration of general-purpose LLMs and VLMs, demonstrating that training-free approaches are viable for 3D-QA and robotic perception in real-world environments.

title: CDAE: Enhancing Perturbation Robustness in Pretrained Language Models with Contrastive Denoising
comment: Submitted to 16th International Conference on Computer and Knowledge Engineering (ICCKE 2026)
summary: Pre-trained language models have significantly improved sentence representation learning, yet their embedding remain sensitive to semantic preserving textual perturbations such as synonym substitution, masking and word dropout. This work proposes a lightweight Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) that refines pre-trained BERT embedding by jointly optimizing contrastive and reconstruction objective to learn perturbation-invariant representation. We evaluate the proposed framework using multiple perturbation strategies with varying strengths and compare it against the original BERT embeddings and SimCSE. Experimental results show that CDAE consistently preserves higher embedding similarity under perturbations, with the improvements becoming more pronounced as framework effectively enhances representation stability while preserving semantic information, highlighting perturbation-invariant learning as a promising direction for improving sentence embeddings. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ComputationIASBS/CDAE

AI.tldr: A lightweight Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) is proposed to refine pre-trained BERT embeddings by jointly optimizing contrastive and reconstruction objectives, making sentence representations invariant to semantic-preserving perturbations. Experiments show CDAE consistently outperforms original BERT and SimCSE in embedding similarity under various perturbation strategies while preserving semantic information.
AI.motivation: Pre-trained language model embeddings remain sensitive to semantic-preserving textual perturbations such as synonym substitution, masking, and word dropout, which harms representation stability and downstream robustness.
AI.method: A lightweight Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) that refines pre-trained BERT embeddings by jointly optimizing two objectives: a contrastive loss to pull perturbed and original representations together, and a reconstruction loss to preserve semantic information.
AI.result: CDAE consistently preserves higher embedding similarity under multiple perturbation strategies with varying strengths, outperforming original BERT embeddings and SimCSE. Improvements become more pronounced with stronger perturbations, while semantic information is preserved.
AI.conclusion: Perturbation-invariant learning is a promising direction for improving sentence embeddings, and CDAE effectively enhances representation stability without sacrificing semantic content. Source code is publicly released.

title: Information Bottleneck Learning for Faithful Time Series Forecasting Explanations
summary: As forecasts increasingly drive decisions in fields such as energy, transportation, and healthcare, understanding the historical data behind these predictions has become as crucial as the predictions themselves. Although existing interpretable-by-design forecasters reveal their internal structures, they offer no guarantee that these structures faithfully reflect the underlying evidence driving the predictions. In contrast, while faithfulness-oriented methods explicitly verify model behavior, they are almost exclusively designed for post-hoc classification tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose IB-Forecast, an inherently interpretable multivariate time-series forecasting framework. It decomposes forecasting into a learned periodic component and a residual component computed with explainable masks over input tokens. With a budget-constrained information bottleneck, end-to-end optimization enables users to directly control explanation sparsity. With a rigorous faithfulness evaluation protocol, extensive experiments demonstrate that IB-Forecast matches the forecasting error of leading black-box models while providing faithful explanations at no additional inference cost. Furthermore, under a matched sparsity budget, these native explanations consistently surpass gradient-based, occlusion-based, and optimization-based baselines across all evaluated datasets. Ultimately, whereas the native explanations of existing interpretable forecasters exhibit poor faithfulness, IB-Forecast guarantees high explanation fidelity, requiring only 14-20% of the observations to deliver low-error predictions.

AI.tldr: IB-Forecast is a novel inherently interpretable multivariate time-series forecasting framework that decomposes forecasting into a learned periodic component and an explainable residual component, using a budget-constrained information bottleneck for controllable explanation sparsity. It matches black-box forecasting accuracy while providing faithful native explanations at no additional inference cost, consistently outperforming existing interpretable forecasters and post-hoc explanation baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing interpretable-by-design forecasters reveal internal structures but do not guarantee faithfulness to the underlying evidence driving predictions. Conversely, faithfulness-oriented methods exist almost exclusively for post-hoc classification tasks. This gap leaves multivariate time-series forecasting without a model that is both inherently interpretable and provably faithful.
AI.method: IB-Forecast decomposes forecasting into (1) a learned periodic component and (2) a residual component computed using explainable masks over input tokens. A budget-constrained information bottleneck is used in end-to-end optimization, allowing users to directly control explanation sparsity. A rigorous faithfulness evaluation protocol is employed to validate explanation fidelity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show IB-Forecast matches the forecasting error of leading black-box models while providing faithful explanations at no additional inference cost. Under matched sparsity budgets, its native explanations consistently outperform gradient-based, occlusion-based, and optimization-based baselines across all evaluated datasets. It requires only 14-20% of observations to achieve low-error predictions.
AI.conclusion: While existing interpretable forecasters exhibit poor explanation faithfulness, IB-Forecast guarantees high explanation fidelity through its inherently interpretable design, providing trustworthy and efficient forecasting for critical decision-making domains.

title: VisualRouter: Query-Grounded Visual Sampling for Long Video Understanding
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have achieved significant progress in video understanding, yet understanding long videos remains challenging due to the large number of visual tokens and limited context windows. Visual sampling provides a practical solution by selecting an informative subset of frames. However, existing methods typically either rely on relevance-aware sampling, leading to redundant frame selection and insufficient temporal coverage, or adopt a fixed sampling strategy regardless of query type. In this paper, we propose VisualRouter, a training-free and plug-and-play framework for query-grounded visual sampling. VisualRouter first classifies each query as either global or local and then applies the corresponding sampling strategy. For global queries, it employs a relevance-coverage hybrid strategy that preserves temporal coverage while retaining query-relevant visual evidence. For local queries, it adopts an event-aware frame selection strategy that performs event partitioning, segment-level frame allocation, and intra-event frame selection, jointly balancing relevance, coverage, and diversity with a limited number of input frames. Experiments show that VisualRouter consistently improves multiple LVLMs over uniform sampling, achieving gains of 5.2%, 7.7%, and 11.6% on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and outperforming existing training-free visual sampling methods under the same setting.

AI.tldr: VisualRouter is a training-free, plug-and-play framework for query-grounded visual sampling in long video understanding with LVLMs. It classifies queries as global or local and applies tailored sampling strategies: a relevance-coverage hybrid for global queries and an event-aware frame selection for local queries. It improves multiple LVLMs over uniform sampling by 5.2%, 7.7%, and 11.6% on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, outperforming existing training-free sampling methods.
AI.motivation: Long video understanding remains challenging due to the large number of visual tokens and limited context windows in LVLMs. Existing visual sampling methods either suffer from redundant frame selection and insufficient temporal coverage (relevance-aware sampling) or apply a fixed sampling strategy regardless of query type, failing to adapt to different information needs.
AI.method: VisualRouter first classifies each query as global or local, then applies the corresponding sampling strategy. For global queries, it uses a relevance-coverage hybrid strategy that maintains temporal coverage while retaining query-relevant visual evidence. For local queries, it employs an event-aware frame selection strategy involving event partitioning, segment-level frame allocation, and intra-event frame selection, jointly balancing relevance, coverage, and diversity with a limited number of input frames.
AI.result: VisualRouter consistently improves multiple LVLMs over uniform sampling, achieving gains of 5.2%, 7.7%, and 11.6% on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and outperforming existing training-free visual sampling methods under identical settings.
AI.conclusion: A query-adaptive, training-free visual sampling framework that distinguishes between global and local queries and applies strategy-specific sampling can significantly improve long video understanding in LVLMs, demonstrating that adapting the sampling strategy to the query type is more effective than fixed or purely relevance-driven approaches.

title: AI and Authenticity in Islamic Research: A Critical Evaluation of Generative AI Reliability, Hallucination, and Source Fidelity in Quranic, Hadith, and Fiqh Knowledge
summary:
Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used by Muslims for religious guidance, Qur'anic interpretation, Hadith explanation, jurisprudential rulings, and Islamic education. Despite its growing adoption, there is limited empirical evidence on whether current AI systems provide authentic, verifiable, and trustworthy Islamic knowledge suitable for high-trust religious contexts. This study evaluates six leading generative AI systems using fifty realistic open-ended Islamic questions covering Qur'anic interpretation, Hadith, Fiqh, ethics, pastoral advice, and Madhhab-sensitive topics. Responses were collected under real-world conditions from participants in Australia and the United Kingdom and analysed using a mixed-method framework examining domain accuracy, citation verification, hallucinations, jurisprudential consistency, uncertainty handling, source provenance, and geographical variation.
  The study addresses four research questions: (1) How accurate and authentic are AI-generated responses across major Islamic knowledge domains? (2) To what extent do AI systems produce hallucinations, incomplete citations, or unverifiable religious references? (3) How consistently do models handle jurisprudential disagreement, Madhhab diversity, and uncertainty? (4) Are current AI systems sufficiently reliable for religious guidance, Islamic education, and scholarly research?
  Overall, current generative AI systems are valuable as assistive tools for introductory Islamic learning but should not be treated as authoritative sources for religious rulings or Islamic research without verification against authenticated primary sources and qualified scholarly expertise. This study provides one of the first comprehensive empirical evaluations of AI reliability within Islamic knowledge, offering practical guidance for researchers, educators, AI developers, and the wider Muslim community.

AI.tldr: This study empirically evaluates six leading generative AI systems using 50 open-ended Islamic questions across Qur'anic interpretation, Hadith, Fiqh, ethics, pastoral advice, and Madhhab-sensitive topics, collected from participants in Australia and the UK. Using a mixed-method framework, the authors assess domain accuracy, citation verification, hallucinations, jurisprudential consistency, uncertainty handling, source provenance, and geographical variation. Findings indicate AI systems are useful assistive tools for introductory Islamic learning but should not be treated as authoritative sources for religious rulings or research without verification against authenticated primary sources and qualified scholarly expertise.
AI.motivation: Despite the growing adoption of generative AI by Muslims for religious guidance and Islamic education, there is limited empirical evidence on whether current AI systems provide authentic, verifiable, and trustworthy Islamic knowledge suitable for high-trust religious contexts. This study fills that gap.
AI.method: Six leading generative AI systems were evaluated using fifty realistic open-ended Islamic questions covering six knowledge domains. Responses were collected under real-world conditions from participants in Australia and the United Kingdom and analysed using a mixed-method framework examining domain accuracy, citation verification, hallucinations, jurisprudential consistency, uncertainty handling, source provenance, and geographical variation. Four research questions guided the evaluation.
AI.result: Current generative AI systems are valuable as assistive tools for introductory Islamic learning but should not be treated as authoritative sources for religious rulings or Islamic research without verification against authenticated primary sources and qualified scholarly expertise.
AI.conclusion: This study provides one of the first comprehensive empirical evaluations of AI reliability within Islamic knowledge, offering practical guidance for researchers, educators, AI developers, and the wider Muslim community regarding the appropriate use and limitations of generative AI in high-trust religious contexts.

title: LM-GRASP: Instance-Specific Language Models for Combinatorial Construction via Online Imitation Learning
summary:
Machine learning for combinatorial optimization typically relies on neural constructors trained via reinforcement learning on large offline datasets for a fixed problem class-incurring high pretraining costs and generalizing poorly outside the training distribution. We propose an alternative: a metaheuristic framework that reformulates the randomized constructive phase of GRASP as an online imitation learning task, trained from scratch on each problem instance. A local search procedure acts as an expert oracle, while a decoder-only Transformer serves as the constructive policy. Unlike classical GRASP, which relies on static, myopic heuristic rules based on localized scalar costs, our approach is fully data-driven: the construction policy emerges from high-quality solutions discovered during the search itself, with no problem-specific feature engineering required.
  We instantiate this as LM-GRASP, a hybrid metaheuristic following an iterative learn-infer-improve cycle, training the policy online via behavioral cloning on a dynamic archive of elite trajectories-no external data or offline pretraining needed. The pipeline interfaces with the domain solely through the objective evaluator used by local search.
  Evaluated on the Taillard PFSP benchmark (ta51-ta60), the most discriminating block due to half its optima being unknown, LM-GRASP outperforms GPU-GRASP by 28.4 makespan units on average-comparable to the gain from GPU acceleration over sequential execution (27.2 units), though with overlapping standard deviations. This suggests instance-specific, online-trained language models are a promising, practical alternative to hand-engineered constructors, especially for landscapes resistant to classical greedy construction.

AI.tldr: LM-GRASP is a metaheuristic framework that reformulates the randomized constructive phase of GRASP as an online imitation learning task, training a decoder-only Transformer from scratch on each problem instance using a local search expert oracle, without offline pretraining or problem-specific feature engineering.
AI.motivation: Neural constructors for combinatorial optimization rely on reinforcement learning with large offline datasets for fixed problem classes, incurring high pretraining costs and poor generalization outside the training distribution. The authors propose an alternative that avoids these costs by learning instance-specific policies online.
AI.method: LM-GRASP follows an iterative learn-infer-improve cycle where a decoder-only Transformer serves as the constructive policy, trained online via behavioral cloning on a dynamic archive of elite trajectories gathered from a local search expert oracle. The pipeline interfaces only through the objective evaluator, requiring no problem-specific feature engineering.
AI.result: On the Taillard PFSP benchmark (ta51-ta60), LM-GRASP outperforms GPU-GRASP by 28.4 makespan units on average, comparable to the gain from GPU acceleration over sequential execution (27.2 units), though with overlapping standard deviations.
AI.conclusion: Instance-specific, online-trained language models are a promising, practical alternative to hand-engineered constructors, especially for optimization landscapes resistant to classical greedy construction.

title: Can Vision-Language Models Reason about AI Edits in Images?
summary: Detection and localization of AI-tampered images are critical for trustworthy AI, yet modern generative models have made such manipulations increasingly difficult to identify. While traditional binary classifiers can detect image tampering, they lack interpretability and generalization. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer a promising alternative due to their strong visual understanding and reasoning capabilities; however, existing approaches typically rely on supervised finetuning with curated explanations rather than exploiting their inherent reasoning capabilities. In this work, we investigate whether VLMs can be trained to reason about AI-generated image edits using reinforcement learning (RL) rather than explicit reasoning supervision. Motivated by the success in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), an RL technique that incentivizes the model to reason by generating thinking traces prior to giving the final answer, we propose a GRPO-based training framework that utilizes simple accuracy and format rewards. Given an input image, the model produces a structured reasoning trace and predicts whether the image has been tampered with. A lightweight segmentation model is then guided by the reasoning output to generate pixel-level localization masks. Experiments across multiple image manipulation datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive detection and localization performance compared to state-of-the-art image forgery detectors, despite requiring substantially weaker supervision. We introduce effective intersection over union (eff-IoU), a unified metric to jointly evaluate detection and localization. These results suggest that reinforcement learning provides an effective and scalable mechanism for teaching VLMs to reason about AI-generated content.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)-based reinforcement learning framework for training Vision-Language Models to detect and localize AI-tampered images. Instead of relying on supervised finetuning with curated explanations, the model learns to generate structured reasoning traces guided only by accuracy and format rewards. A lightweight segmentation model uses these reasoning outputs to produce pixel-level localization masks. The approach achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forgery detectors with substantially weaker supervision, and introduces a unified eff-IoU metric for jointly evaluating detection and localization.
AI.motivation: AI-tampered image detection is increasingly difficult due to modern generative models. Traditional binary classifiers lack interpretability and generalization, while existing VLM-based approaches require supervised finetuning with curated explanations, failing to exploit VLMs' inherent reasoning capabilities. This paper investigates whether reinforcement learning can teach VLMs to reason about AI-generated edits without explicit reasoning supervision.
AI.method: The method applies GRPO, a reinforcement learning technique that incentivizes models to reason by generating thinking traces before producing final answers. The framework uses simple accuracy and format rewards: given an input image, the VLM produces a structured reasoning trace and predicts tampering status. A lightweight segmentation model is then guided by the reasoning output to generate pixel-level localization masks. The paper also introduces eff-IoU, a unified metric combining detection and localization evaluation.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple image manipulation datasets show the proposed approach achieves competitive detection and localization performance compared to state-of-the-art image forgery detectors, despite requiring substantially weaker supervision (no curated reasoning labels).
AI.conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides an effective and scalable mechanism for teaching VLMs to reason about AI-generated content, suggesting a promising direction beyond supervised finetuning for interpretable and generalizable forgery detection.

title: Operationally Guided Placement-Aware Learning for Industrial Online 3D Bin Packing
summary: The online three-dimensional bin packing problem (3D-BPP) is a longstanding challenge in logistics and industrial palletizing. Recent learning-based methods use a learned policy to select among feasible candidate placements. Performance depends on the candidate generator and representation, especially in industrial settings where packings must be space-efficient, stable, compact, and balanced. However, prior work has mainly optimized the policy, while candidate generation and representation remain largely geometry-driven. We address this gap with OPAL, an operationally guided placement-aware learning framework for industrial online 3D-BPP which combines an Operationally Guided Empty-Maximal-Space generator (OG-EMS), an operational representation for each candidate placement, and a masked ranking policy trained with proximal policy optimization. OG-EMS evaluates multiple anchors within each free-space region and prioritizes low, well-supported, compact, and spatially diverse placements. An xLSTM-based Placement Encoder models dependencies among geometric and operational candidate attributes, while a lightweight recurrent core combines the resulting embeddings with the current item and pallet state to rank feasible actions. On the BED-BPP benchmark, OPAL achieves a mean space utilization of 0.49, with improvements of 15.1% from operationally guided candidate generation and 6.3% from learned ranking, while maintaining robust inference-time performance.

AI.tldr: OPAL is an operationally guided placement-aware learning framework for industrial online 3D-BPP that combines an Operationally Guided Empty-Maximal-Space generator (OG-EMS), an xLSTM-based Placement Encoder for candidate representation, and a masked ranking policy trained with PPO. It achieves a mean space utilization of 0.49 on the BED-BPP benchmark, with 15.1% improvement from guided candidate generation and 6.3% from learned ranking.
AI.motivation: Prior learning-based 3D-BPP methods focused mainly on optimizing the placement policy while candidate generation and representation remained geometry-driven. In industrial settings, packings must also be stable, compact, and balanced—operational factors that existing approaches largely ignore at the candidate generation and representation stage.
AI.method: OPAL consists of three components: (1) OG-EMS, an operationally guided candidate generator that evaluates multiple anchors within each free-space region and prioritizes low, well-supported, compact, and spatially diverse placements; (2) an xLSTM-based Placement Encoder that models dependencies among geometric and operational candidate attributes; and (3) a lightweight recurrent core combining embeddings with current item and pallet state, trained via a masked ranking policy using proximal policy optimization (PPO).
AI.result: On the BED-BPP benchmark, OPAL achieves a mean space utilization of 0.49, with a 15.1% improvement attributable to operationally guided candidate generation and a 6.3% improvement from learned ranking, while maintaining robust inference-time performance.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly incorporating operational guidance into candidate generation and representation, rather than only optimizing the policy, yields substantial gains in space utilization for industrial online 3D-BPP, demonstrating the importance of a holistic learning framework that addresses all stages of the pipeline.

authors: Jacobus G. M. van der Linden
title: Search Strategies for Optimal Classification and Regression Trees
summary: Optimal decision trees (ODTs) are compact, interpretable machine learning models that globally optimize a given objective, but their scalability remains challenging. While recent work has proposed a variety of search strategies to improve scalability, the precise contribution of each strategy remains unclear. To address this gap, we introduce a general algorithmic framework for ODTs that instantiates previously used search strategies and enables the definition of new ones. This provides a common lens through which to understand and compare different strategies, which we use to empirically investigate the effect of 18 search strategies. Compared to the state of the art, the best strategy in our evaluation achieves significantly better anytime performance for classification, and improves runtime by more than an order of magnitude for regression.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a general algorithmic framework for optimal decision trees (ODTs) that unifies previously used search strategies and enables new ones, allowing systematic empirical comparison of 18 search strategies. The best strategy significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in anytime performance for classification and improves regression runtime by over an order of magnitude.
AI.motivation: Optimal decision trees are valuable for their compactness and interpretability, but scalability remains a major challenge. While various search strategies have been proposed to improve ODT scalability, the precise contribution of each strategy is unclear due to lack of a common comparison framework.
AI.method: The authors design a general algorithmic framework for ODTs that can instantiate previously used search strategies and supports the definition of new ones. This framework serves as a unified lens to systematically compare and understand the contributions of 18 different search strategies.
AI.result: The best strategy from the evaluation achieves significantly better anytime performance for classification compared to state-of-the-art methods, and improves runtime by more than an order of magnitude for regression tasks.
AI.conclusion: A unified algorithmic framework can clarify the contributions of different ODT search strategies, and the identified best strategy substantially improves scalability for both classification and regression tasks.

title: Towards Real-Time PixOOD: Efficient Anomaly Segmentation for Autonomous Vehicles
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Efficient Deep Learning: Methods and Applications workshop, 35th International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN 2026)
summary: Real-time anomaly segmentation is essential for the safety of autonomous systems. Although recent approaches offer high accuracy, their computational cost limits their deployment on embedded hardware. This work presents an efficient and accelerated pipeline designed for both embedded and desktop platforms, targeting the autonomous driving and railway domains. The proposed approach reformulates the Neyman-Pearson scoring stage of PixOOD, a state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection method, and deploys the full pipeline through hardware-optimized TensorRT compilation, reaching up to 182 FPS on a desktop NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU and 75 FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin embedded platform, respectively 20x and 18x faster than the original baseline. The achieved results demonstrate that advanced anomaly segmentation can be efficiently deployed for onboard processing in autonomous driving and railway applications.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an efficient and accelerated anomaly segmentation pipeline for real-time autonomous driving and railway applications. By reformulating the Neyman-Pearson scoring stage of the PixOOD out-of-distribution detection method and deploying it via hardware-optimized TensorRT compilation, the approach achieves 182 FPS on a desktop RTX 4060 GPU and 75 FPS on the Jetson AGX Orin embedded platform, representing 20x and 18x speedups over the original baseline.
AI.motivation: Real-time anomaly segmentation is critical for autonomous system safety, but existing high-accuracy methods are computationally prohibitive for deployment on embedded hardware. The authors aim to bridge the gap between accuracy and deployability.
AI.method: The approach reformulates the Neyman-Pearson scoring stage of PixOOD, a state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection method, and deploys the entire pipeline through hardware-optimized TensorRT compilation targeting both embedded (Jetson AGX Orin) and desktop (RTX 4060) platforms.
AI.result: The optimized pipeline reaches up to 182 FPS on a desktop NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU and 75 FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin embedded platform, achieving 20x and 18x speedups respectively compared to the original baseline.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate that advanced anomaly segmentation can be efficiently deployed for onboard processing in both autonomous driving and railway applications, validating the feasibility of running state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection in real time on embedded platforms.

title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search for Constraint Model Reformulation to Improve Solver Efficiency
summary: Combinatorial problems appear in numerous industrial applications. A common approach is to formulate these problems as declarative constraint models that can subsequently be compiled to and solved by a range of back-end solvers. Recent work shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can produce correct models from natural language, but even a correct model can be expensive to solve because performance remains sensitive to modelling choices. In this work, we investigate whether LLMs can automate performance-oriented model reformulation. Inspired by Automatic Heuristic Design (AHD), we use an evolutionary framework in which an LLM proposes candidate reformulations that are verified and benchmarked against the user-defined baseline model. We compare AHD-adapted search strategies that control which prior attempts, instructions, and measured feedback enter each prompt. Existing retention strategies prioritize recency or performance, but do not explicitly diversify the context. To cover this gap, we introduce Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR), which applies Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) to instance-level runtime vectors to retain behaviourally diverse attempts. We systematically evaluate the strategies on eight CSPLib problems using validation-based final model selection. The results show that: (i) iterative reformulation can produce substantial held-out speedups; (ii) strategies that keep the retained context diverse outperform those that retain only recent or the fastest attempts; and (iii) validation-based selection improves the held-out speedup of every strategy.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether LLMs can automate performance-oriented reformulation of combinatorial constraint models. Using an evolutionary framework inspired by Automatic Heuristic Design, the authors introduce Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR)—a strategy applying Maximal Marginal Relevance to runtime vectors for behaviorally diverse context retention. Evaluated on eight CSPLib problems, iterative reformulation yields substantial speedups, diverse retention outperforms recency/performance-based strategies, and validation-based selection consistently improves held-out results.
AI.motivation: Although LLMs can generate correct constraint models from natural language, model performance remains highly sensitive to modeling choices, and even correct models can be expensive to solve. The authors seek to automate performance-oriented model reformulation to overcome this bottleneck.
AI.method: The approach uses an evolutionary framework where an LLM proposes candidate reformulations that are verified and benchmarked against a user-defined baseline. Multiple search strategies control which prior attempts, instructions, and measured feedback enter each prompt. The novel Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR) strategy applies Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) to instance-level runtime vectors to retain behaviorally diverse attempts. Four search strategies are systematically compared on eight CSPLib problems with validation-based final model selection.
AI.result: (i) Iterative reformulation produces substantial held-out speedups; (ii) strategies that keep the retained context diverse outperform those retaining only recent or fastest attempts; (iii) validation-based selection improves held-out speedup for every strategy.
AI.conclusion: LLMs can effectively automate performance-oriented model reformulation within an evolutionary framework, and explicitly diversifying the retained context via instance-level behavioral diversity is key to superior performance across held-out instances.

title: Multi-channel Uplift Policy Learning
summary: E-commerce platforms must allocate fixed marketing budgets across multiple channels to maximize business utility. However, standard predict-then-optimize (PTO) paradigms fail in this compositional space due to observational confounding and severe extrapolation. We formulate this challenge as a simplex-constrained uplift decision problem and propose ReAlloc, a fast-slow causal framework. Specifically, an agile Orthogonal Teacher extracts unbiased local gradients from short-term logs, while an Explanation-Guided Student distills them into a structured marginal field over long-term horizons. This design enables support-aware, conservative decisions that capture cross-channel substitutions. Extensive simulations and large-scale online A/B tests on Taobao platform demonstrate that ReAlloc achieves simultaneous lifts in both pay order and income.

AI.tldr: ReAlloc is a fast-slow causal framework that solves the simplex-constrained uplift decision problem for allocating fixed marketing budgets across e-commerce channels, addressing observational confounding and extrapolation in compositional spaces. It uses an Orthogonal Teacher to extract unbiased local gradients and an Explanation-Guided Student to distill them into a structured long-term marginal field, achieving simultaneous gains in pay orders and income in Taobao A/B tests.
AI.motivation: Standard predict-then-optimize (PTO) paradigms fail in compositional e-commerce budget allocation spaces due to observational confounding and severe extrapolation, necessitating a new approach for allocating fixed marketing budgets across multiple channels to maximize business utility.
AI.method: The paper formulates budget allocation as a simplex-constrained uplift decision problem and proposes ReAlloc, a fast-slow causal framework. An agile Orthogonal Teacher extracts unbiased local gradients from short-term logs, while an Explanation-Guided Student distills these into a structured marginal field over long-term horizons, enabling support-aware, conservative decisions capturing cross-channel substitutions.
AI.result: Extensive simulations and large-scale online A/B tests on the Taobao platform demonstrate that ReAlloc achieves simultaneous lifts in both pay order and income.
AI.conclusion: ReAlloc effectively addresses the compositional budget allocation problem by providing support-aware, conservative decisions that account for cross-channel substitutions, validated by both simulation and real-world online experiments.

title: AuricularWorld: Hierarchical Action-Guided World Modeling for Fine-Grained Auricular Structure Segmentation from CT Scans
summary: Fine-grained segmentation of auricular structures in CT is challenging because the ear occupies a small image region, cartilage boundaries are highly irregular, and interfaces between cartilage and surrounding soft tissues are often ambiguous. Clinical annotations may also include both composite structures containing cartilage and adjacent skin and their corresponding cartilage-only regions, producing nested and overlapping labels. We propose a world-model-based segmentation framework that enables iterative anatomical reasoning beyond conventional feed-forward prediction. Built on an encoder-decoder architecture, the framework introduces a deterministic recurrent state-space model into the intermediate latent space. Multi-scale encoder features and partially decoded representations are fused to form a structural observation that initializes the latent dynamics. During inference, the model performs a three-step latent rollout without ground-truth guidance. Hierarchical anatomical actions update the recurrent state and progressively refine the latent representation. The resulting latent trajectory is projected back into the decoder and combined with high-resolution features to produce the final segmentation. To learn reliable latent transitions, we introduce a balanced hierarchical action objective that addresses foreground sparsity, missing anatomical groups, and imbalance between add and remove operations. Extensive experiments show that the proposed framework consistently improves segmentation accuracy and reduces HD95 by more than 43% for small, irregular, and overlapping auricular structures in CT. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of latent world-model reasoning for challenging medical image segmentation.

AI.tldr: A world-model-based segmentation framework using a deterministic recurrent state-space model in the latent space of an encoder-decoder, enabling iterative anatomical reasoning for fine-grained auricular CT segmentation. It reduces HD95 by over 43% on small, irregular, and overlapping ear structures.
AI.motivation: Fine-grained auricular segmentation in CT is difficult due to the small anatomical region, highly irregular cartilage boundaries, ambiguous cartilage-soft tissue interfaces, and nested/overlapping clinical labels for composite and cartilage-only structures—all of which challenge conventional feed-forward segmentation models.
AI.method: Built on an encoder-decoder architecture, the framework inserts a deterministic recurrent state-space model into the intermediate latent space. Multi-scale encoder features and partially decoded representations are fused to form a structural observation that initializes latent dynamics. During inference, a three-step latent rollout (without ground-truth guidance) applies hierarchical anatomical actions to update the recurrent state and refine the latent representation. The latent trajectory is projected back into the decoder and merged with high-resolution features for final segmentation. A balanced hierarchical action objective handles foreground sparsity, missing anatomical groups, and add/remove imbalance.
AI.result: The framework consistently improves segmentation accuracy and reduces HD95 by more than 43% for small, irregular, and overlapping auricular structures in CT, demonstrating robust gains over conventional feed-forward approaches.
AI.conclusion: Latent world-model reasoning is effective for challenging medical image segmentation, particularly for anatomically small, irregularly shaped, and overlapping structures, and offers a promising paradigm beyond single-pass feed-forward predictions.

title: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
summary: Retrieving past experiences has become a common strategy to enhance large language model agents. However, most existing memory-augmented agents treat retrieved experiences as static records to be replayed verbatim, injecting them into the context regardless of whether they align with the agent's current situation. This ``replay'' paradigm ignores the gap between the abstract, general nature of stored experience and the concrete, ever-changing states encountered at decision time, frequently causing negative transfer. In contrast, humans rarely recall past experiences verbatim; instead, they reorganize and adapt retrieved memories to fit the present context. Inspired by this, we propose MemHarness, a framework that equips LLM agents to actively harness and reconstruct past experiences based on the present context. At each decision step, a unified policy model critiques and reconstructs the retrieved experience conditioned on the current state, producing context-grounded guidance before acting. This reconstructive ability emerges naturally through end-to-end training with GRPO. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show that MemHarness substantially outperforms pure RL and static memory-augmented baselines, demonstrating strong robustness in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. Furthermore, our analyses reveal that this reconstruction objective not only prevents negative transfer but also serves as latent guidance during training, fundamentally improving the agent's intrinsic reasoning capabilities.

AI.tldr: MemHarness is a framework that enables LLM agents to actively reconstruct and adapt retrieved past experiences to fit the current context, rather than replaying them verbatim, substantially outperforming static memory-augmented baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop.
AI.motivation: Existing memory-augmented agents replay retrieved experiences verbatim, ignoring the gap between abstract stored experiences and concrete current states, which frequently causes negative transfer. Humans, in contrast, reorganize and adapt memories to fit present contexts, motivating a reconstructive approach.
AI.method: MemHarness uses a unified policy model that critiques and reconstructs retrieved experiences conditioned on the current state at each decision step, producing context-grounded guidance before acting. The reconstructive ability emerges through end-to-end training with GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization).
AI.result: Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show MemHarness substantially outperforms pure RL and static memory-augmented baselines, demonstrating strong robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios. Analyses show the reconstruction objective prevents negative transfer and serves as latent guidance during training, improving intrinsic reasoning capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The reconstruction objective not only prevents negative transfer from irrelevant memories but also fundamentally improves the agent's intrinsic reasoning capabilities through latent guidance during training, making MemHarness a robust alternative to static memory replay paradigms.

title: Persistent Gaussian Perturbations Prevent Oversmoothing in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks
summary: Oversmoothing is a fundamental limitation of deep graph neural networks (GNNs), where repeated message passing causes node representations to become increasingly similar, eventually collapsing toward a low-dimensional subspace. This phenomenon limits the effective depth of message-passing architectures and motivates the search for mechanisms that preserve representation diversity. In this paper, we study a recurrent graph neural network in which independent Gaussian noise is injected after every propagation step and analyze the resulting architecture as a stochastic dynamical system. Under a standard global contraction assumption on the deterministic update, we prove that the hidden representations form a geometrically ergodic Markov chain admitting a unique invariant probability measure. Our main theoretical result establishes an explicit positive lower bound on the expected stationary Dirichlet energy, proportional to both the noise variance and the spectral gap of the underlying graph. Consequently, the stationary representations cannot collapse onto the constant manifold, providing a rigorous guarantee that asymptotic oversmoothing is prevented in the sense of non-vanishing Dirichlet energy. Our analysis reveals persistent stochastic perturbations as a fundamentally different mechanism for combating oversmoothing, complementing existing deterministic approaches based on residual connections, normalization, and graph rewiring. Finally, numerical experiments on both linear and nonlinear recurrent graph neural networks closely match the theoretical predictions, illustrating the emergence of a stationary distribution and the predicted dependence of the limiting Dirichlet energy on the noise intensity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies recurrent graph neural networks with injected Gaussian noise after each propagation step, analyzing them as stochastic dynamical systems. Under a global contraction assumption, the hidden representations form a geometrically ergodic Markov chain with a unique invariant measure, and the expected stationary Dirichlet energy has an explicit positive lower bound proportional to noise variance and the graph's spectral gap, guaranteeing asymptotic oversmoothing is prevented.
AI.motivation: Oversmoothing limits the effective depth of message-passing GNNs, where repeated propagation collapses node representations toward a low-dimensional subspace. The paper seeks mechanisms that preserve representation diversity, proposing persistent stochastic perturbations as an alternative to deterministic approaches like residual connections, normalization, and graph rewiring.
AI.method: The researchers inject independent Gaussian noise after every propagation step in a recurrent GNN and analyze the architecture as a stochastic dynamical system. They prove the hidden representations form a geometrically ergodic Markov chain with a unique invariant probability measure under a standard global contraction assumption on the deterministic update, and derive an explicit lower bound on the expected stationary Dirichlet energy proportional to both noise variance and the spectral gap of the underlying graph.
AI.result: The main theoretical result establishes a positive lower bound on the expected stationary Dirichlet energy, proving the stationary representations cannot collapse onto the constant manifold. Numerical experiments on linear and nonlinear recurrent GNNs closely match the theoretical predictions, showing the emergence of a stationary distribution and the predicted dependence of limiting Dirichlet energy on noise intensity.
AI.conclusion: Persistent stochastic perturbations represent a fundamentally different mechanism for combating oversmoothing, providing rigorous guarantees that asymptotic oversmoothing is prevented in the sense of non-vanishing Dirichlet energy, complementing existing deterministic approaches.

title: RefCaptioner: Multi-Reference Image-Grounded Video Captioning
summary: Existing video captioning models generate natural descriptions of video content but cannot explicitly ground local visual elements to multiple reference images. We introduce multi-reference image-grounded video captioning, a new task requiring factual video descriptions with phrase-level reference grounding, and propose RefCaptioner, a two-stage post-training framework for this task. RefCaptioner combines mixed-data SFT with Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO to jointly improve reference selection, phrase-level binding, distractor rejection, and cross-reference consistency while preserving general video-captioning ability. To support training, we construct a corpus containing $20,000$ videos and 171,354 reference images. We further introduce MRVBench, a benchmark for evaluating caption factuality and multi-reference grounding on both real-world and AI-generated videos. Experiments show that RefCaptioner achieves the best overall performance among the open-source models while remaining competitive on standard video captioning benchmarks. Human evaluation further confirms that its captions are preferred by annotators and enable more source-faithful video reconstruction with both open-source and proprietary video generators.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces multi-reference image-grounded video captioning, a new task where video descriptions must be grounded to specific reference images with phrase-level alignment. The authors propose RefCaptioner, a two-stage post-training framework combining mixed-data SFT with Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO to jointly improve reference selection, phrase-level binding, distractor rejection, and cross-reference consistency. They construct a training corpus of 20,000 videos and 171,354 reference images, introduce the MRVBench benchmark, and demonstrate state-of-the-art performance among open-source models on both the new task and standard captioning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing video captioning models can describe video content but cannot explicitly anchor local visual elements to multiple reference images, limiting their ability to produce source-faithful, reference-grounded descriptions needed for applications like video reconstruction and multimodal understanding.
AI.method: RefCaptioner uses a two-stage post-training framework: (1) mixed-data supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to establish basic grounding and captioning ability, and (2) Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO, a reinforcement learning approach that jointly optimizes reference selection, phrase-level binding, distractor rejection, and cross-reference consistency while preserving general video-captioning capability. A large-scale corpus with 20,000 videos and 171,354 reference images is constructed for training, and MRVBench is introduced for evaluation.
AI.result: RefCaptioner achieves the best overall performance among open-source models on both MRVBench and standard video captioning benchmarks. Human evaluation shows annotators prefer its captions, and generated captions enable more source-faithful video reconstruction with both open-source and proprietary video generators.
AI.conclusion: Multi-reference image-grounded video captioning is a feasible and valuable task, and RefCaptioner demonstrates that a two-stage post-training approach with targeted reinforcement learning can achieve strong reference grounding while maintaining general video captioning quality, benefiting downstream applications like video reconstruction.

title: Tycho: Active Abstraction with Programmatic World Models for ARC-AGI-3
comment: 52 pages, 18 figures, 17 tables. Open-source implementation: https://github.com/NIMI-research/Tycho
summary:
ARC-AGI-3 turns abstraction into an interactive problem of skill acquisition. A player must infer an unfamiliar game's rules, hidden state, and goal while maintaining action efficiency because every move counts. We formalize these environments as parameterized rendered deterministic Moore machines and introduce Tycho, a coding-agent system that constructs and uses game-specific models during interaction. Tycho separates actionable observations from intermediate animation, level-completion, and game-over frames. From this structured history, an agent can model, test, plan with, repair, or bypass a free-form executable hypothesis.
  In one matched public-set run per policy, we compare four orchestration policies on all 25 public games using Claude Opus 4.8 under matched inference budgets. Actor-requested delegation to a model builder obtains the highest observed mean Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), 88.49. With this selected policy, GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 both reach 100.00 RHAE and complete all 183 levels. Their game-balanced first-run human-replay midranks are 98.5 and 100.0. Opus 5 uses 61% fewer scored actions than the aggregate official human baselines.
  Automatic repair after verification failures produces models that reproduce observed transitions much more accurately, yet reaches only 83.07 RHAE. Transition match indicates whether a simulator reproduces observed dynamics, not whether it has identified the objective or improves the next action. Strong play also requires deciding when to construct, repair, use, or bypass a model. We call this joint problem active abstraction: generating a testable model from costly interaction and deciding when acquiring or using it is worth its cost.

AI.tldr: ARC-AGI-3 reformulates abstraction as an interactive skill-acquisition problem where players infer rules, hidden state, and goals under strict action-efficiency constraints. The paper introduces Tycho, a coding-agent system that constructs and uses game-specific executable models during interaction, and demonstrates that actor-requested delegation to a model builder achieves the highest action efficiency (88.49 RHAE), with top models (GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5) reaching perfect 100.00 RHAE across all 183 levels.
AI.motivation: Abstraction in interactive environments requires deciding not only how to model the world but also when constructing, repairing, using, or bypassing a model is worth its cost—termed "active abstraction"—since every action counts and action efficiency is a key measure of performance.
AI.method: Environments are formalized as parameterized rendered deterministic Moore machines. Tycho is a coding-agent pipeline that separates actionable observations from intermediate animation, level-completion, and game-over frames, and supports modeling, testing, planning with, repairing, or bypassing a free-form executable hypothesis. Four orchestration policies are compared across 25 public games using Claude Opus 4.8 under matched inference budgets.
AI.result: Actor-requested delegation to a model builder achieves the highest mean RHAE of 88.49. With this policy, GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 both reach 100.00 RHAE and complete all 183 levels, with game-balanced first-run human-replay midranks of 98.5 and 100.0. Opus 5 uses 61% fewer scored actions than aggregate official human baselines. Automatic repair reaches only 83.07 RHAE, demonstrating that transition match alone does not guarantee objective identification or improved next-action decisions.
AI.conclusion: Effective interactive abstraction requires jointly solving two problems: generating testable models from costly interaction, and deciding when model acquisition or usage is worth its cost. Transition fidelity is insufficient; strong play also demands strategic decisions about when to construct, repair, use, or bypass a model.

title: TopoFormer: Topology Meets Attention for Graph Learning
summary: We introduce Topoformer, a lightweight and scalable framework for graph representation learning that encodes topological structure into attention-friendly sequences. At the core of our method is Topo-Scan, a novel module that decomposes a graph into a short, ordered sequence of topological tokens by slicing over node or edge filtrations. These sequences capture multi-scale structural patterns, from local motifs to global organization, and are processed by a Transformer to produce expressive graph-level embeddings. Unlike traditional persistent homology pipelines, Topo-Scan is parallelizable, avoids costly diagram computations, and integrates seamlessly with standard deep learning architectures. We provide theoretical guarantees on the stability of our topological encodings and demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across graph classification and molecular property prediction benchmarks. Our results show that Topoformer matches or exceeds strong GNN and topology-based baselines while offering predictable and efficient compute. This work opens a new path for parallelizable and unifying approaches to graph representation learning that integrate topological inductive biases into attention frameworks.

AI.tldr: Topoformer is a lightweight graph representation learning framework that encodes topological structure into attention-friendly sequences via Topo-Scan, a module that decomposes graphs into ordered topological tokens from node/edge filtrations. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on graph classification and molecular property prediction while being parallelizable and efficient, avoiding costly persistent homology computations.
AI.motivation: Traditional persistent homology pipelines are computationally expensive and difficult to integrate with deep learning architectures. The authors aim to provide a scalable, parallelizable approach that injects topological inductive biases into attention-based frameworks for graph representation learning.
AI.method: Topoformer introduces Topo-Scan, which slices a graph over node or edge filtrations to produce ordered sequences of topological tokens capturing multi-scale structural patterns. These tokens are fed into a Transformer to generate expressive graph-level embeddings, replacing traditional persistence diagram computations.
AI.result: Topoformer matches or exceeds strong GNN and topology-based baselines on graph classification and molecular property prediction benchmarks, with theoretical stability guarantees and predictable, efficient compute.
AI.conclusion: This work opens a new path for parallelizable and unifying graph representation learning by seamlessly integrating topological inductive biases into attention frameworks.

title: Beyond Frame Selection: Generative Latent Evidence Aggregation for Long-Video Understanding
summary: Long-video understanding commonly compresses videos into a small set of frames or visual tokens for answer generation. Existing compact pipelines focus on retaining relevant visual content as explicit evidence. Yet making evidence available does not ensure that complementary cues across moments are integrated for answering. Our key idea is to organize selected frames into query-relevant cross-frame evidence before generation. We formulate this post-selection stage as a latent evidence interface and instantiate it with GenEvA ($\textbf{Gen}erative$ $Latent$ $\textbf{Ev}idence$ $\textbf{A}ggregation$), a distribution-guided latent evidence aggregation framework. Specifically, GenEvA uses a query-conditioned evidence distribution to focus aggregation on relevant frames, forming compact cross-frame latent evidence from their frame-specific information. Since cross-frame integration is not always needed, the same distribution determines whether to insert this latent complement. Across four benchmarks and two Video-MLLM backbones, GenEvA consistently improves matched-frame baselines. At 8 frames, it raises the four-benchmark LLaVA-Video average by $+5.2$ points and Qwen2.5-VL accuracy on LVBench by $+10.1$ points. These gains require only $0.11\%$--$0.40\%$ average video-token overhead; analyses further show task-aware allocation and benefits from Adaptive Evidence Invocation.

AI.tldr: GenEvA is a generative latent evidence aggregation framework that organizes query-relevant cross-frame evidence after frame selection in long-video understanding, using a query-conditioned evidence distribution to decide when and how to integrate complementary cues across frames.
AI.motivation: Existing compact video understanding pipelines retain relevant visual content as explicit evidence but fail to ensure complementary cues across different moments are integrated for answering; making evidence available does not guarantee it is effectively combined.
AI.method: GenEvA formulates post-selection cross-frame aggregation as a latent evidence interface. It uses a query-conditioned evidence distribution to focus aggregation on relevant frames, forming compact cross-frame latent evidence from frame-specific information. The same distribution determines adaptively whether latent complement insertion is needed (Adaptive Evidence Invocation).
AI.result: Across four benchmarks and two Video-MLLM backbones, GenEvA consistently improves matched-frame baselines. At 8 frames, it raises LLaVA-Video four-benchmark average by +5.2 points and Qwen2.5-VL accuracy on LVBench by +10.1 points, with only 0.11%-0.40% average video-token overhead.
AI.conclusion: GenEvA demonstrates that explicitly aggregating cross-frame evidence in the latent space, guided by query relevance, yields substantial gains over simply selecting relevant frames. Task-aware allocation and adaptive evidence invocation further enhance performance with negligible overhead.

title: One Human, $N$ Agents: Audit-Budget Allocation for LLM Agent Fleets under Miscalibrated, Correlated Confidence
summary: A single human must audit $N$ LLM agents under a budget of $B \ll N$ audits per round, guided by self-reported confidence that may be adversarially miscalibrated and by correlated errors. We model this as budgeted noisy inspection over a two-level Gaussian copula and locate the miscalibration threshold $δ^*$ past which confidence-ranked auditing is \emph{worse} than random. Two a-priori expectations reverse: $δ^*$ \emph{rises} as the budget shrinks, and cross-family correlation is not low---shared difficulty dominates lineage. Five open-weight LLMs show operationally useless (near-constant) confidence, point estimates at or beyond the flip though CIs straddle it; a proprietary model is informative and lands below it. We give a quantitative criterion for \emph{vacuous} oversight, and replaying policies on recorded traces confirms the ordering.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes budgeted human auditing of LLM agents, modeling it as noisy inspection over a two-level Gaussian copula. It identifies a miscalibration threshold δ* beyond which confidence-ranked auditing performs worse than random auditing. Counterintuitively, δ* rises as the budget shrinks, and cross-family correlation is dominated by shared difficulty rather than lineage. Five open-weight LLMs show operationally useless near-constant confidence with estimates at/above the flip threshold, while a proprietary model is informative and below it. A quantitative criterion for vacuous oversight is provided, and policy replays on recorded traces confirm the ordering.
AI.motivation: The work addresses the practical challenge of a single human auditor overseeing many LLM agents with limited audit budget, needing to determine when self-reported confidence from agents is trustworthy for prioritization versus when it becomes actively worse than random auditing.
AI.method: The author models budgeted noisy inspection using a two-level Gaussian copula to capture both miscalibration of self-reported confidence and correlated errors among agents. Analytical derivation locates the miscalibration threshold δ*, followed by empirical evaluation on five open-weight LLMs and one proprietary model.
AI.result: The analysis reveals two reversed expectations: δ* increases as the audit budget shrinks, and cross-family correlation is not low—shared difficulty dominates lineage. Open-weight LLMs exhibit near-constant (operationally useless) confidence with point estimates at or beyond δ* (with CIs straddling it), while the proprietary model shows informative confidence below the threshold. Recorded-trace policy replays confirm the theoretical ordering.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a quantitative criterion for detecting vacuous oversight and demonstrates that confidence-ranked auditing can be worse than random under adversarial miscalibration, with practical implications for choosing which LLM agents can be safely supervised under budget constraints.

title: HARGO: Heterogeneity-Aware Reward-Guided Optimization for RL Post-Training of LLMs on HPC Tasks
summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can equip large language models (LLMs) with domain knowledge for high-performance computing (HPC) tasks such as data race detection and benchmark question answering. However, knowledge alone does not guarantee task-appropriate behavior: the same SFT model that correctly classifies 88.65\% of C/C++ data race samples produces verbose, imprecise answers to factual queries, with 65.9\% of MLPerf responses exceeding 40 characters. Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training addresses this gap by optimizing for task-specific rewards rather than token-level imitation. Yet HPC tasks exhibit extreme heterogeneity, with binary classification, factual QA, and semantic generation differing by 58x in answer length, spanning three distinct reward distributions, and showing widely varying SFT accuracy. This makes uniform-weight RL methods such as GRPO suboptimal. We propose HARGO, Heterogeneity-Aware Reward-Guided Optimization, which introduces per-response importance weighting via confidence-modulated advantage: computing a discrimination signal from group-level reward contrast and a confidence signal from reference model log-probabilities, then modulating the advantage before computing per-response weights, without requiring task-type labels. Across four HPC tasks and nine methods, HARGO achieves the best performance on all three primary metrics: WinRate 54.62\%, Data Race F1 91.30\%, and PLP Similarity 0.8558. Ablation confirms complementary contributions from both signals. HARGO establishes the best overall alignment quality among compared methods for heterogeneous HPC tasks.

AI.tldr: HARGO is a heterogeneity-aware reinforcement learning post-training method that improves LLM alignment for diverse HPC tasks by computing confidence-modulated advantages with per-response importance weighting, outperforming nine baselines across four tasks on all three primary metrics.
AI.motivation: Supervised fine-tuning alone gives LLMs domain knowledge for HPC tasks but fails to produce task-appropriate behavior (e.g., verbose, imprecise answers). HPC tasks exhibit extreme heterogeneity—varying by 58x in answer length, spanning three reward distributions, and differing in SFT accuracy—making uniform-weight RL methods like GRPO suboptimal.
AI.method: HARGO introduces per-response importance weighting via confidence-modulated advantage. It computes a discrimination signal from group-level reward contrast and a confidence signal from reference model log-probabilities, then modulates the advantage before computing per-response weights, without requiring task-type labels.
AI.result: Across four HPC tasks and nine methods, HARGO achieves the best performance on all three primary metrics: WinRate 54.62%, Data Race F1 91.30%, and PLP Similarity 0.8558. Ablation confirms complementary contributions from both signals.
AI.conclusion: HARGO establishes the best overall alignment quality among compared methods for heterogeneous HPC tasks, demonstrating that heterogeneity-aware reward-guided optimization effectively addresses the limitations of uniform-weight RL post-training in multi-task HPC settings.

title: What to Remove, What to Preserve: Dual-Ambiguity Rectification for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: All-in-one image restoration aims to handle diverse degradations within a unified framework. Existing methods commonly encode heterogeneous degradation conditions in a shared latent space, where degradation-related cues and scene content can remain entangled. We characterize the resulting challenge as dual ambiguity: semantic ambiguity in channel-wise modulation and spatial ambiguity in restoration responses, which can lead to content corruption and residual artifacts. To mitigate this issue, we propose DAR-Net, a Dual-Ambiguity Rectification Network for all-in-one image restoration. DAR-Net first introduces a Degradation Archetype Representation (DAR) module to construct a structured degradation state through simplex-constrained archetype mixture modeling. Based on this state, a Semantic Ambiguity Rectification (SeAR) module generates degradation-aware prompts to improve channel-wise conditioning in the decoder. A Spatial Ambiguity Rectification (SpAR) module further regularizes degradation-aware and complementary features toward orthogonal response subspaces, reducing spatial interference between removal and preservation cues. Extensive experiments on standard all-in-one restoration benchmarks show that DAR-Net achieves the best overall performance under both three-degradation and five-degradation settings, improving the average PSNR over the strongest competitor by 0.14 dB and 0.34 dB, respectively; it additionally shows superior performance on CDD-11 and WeatherBench.

AI.tldr: DAR-Net, a Dual-Ambiguity Rectification Network for all-in-one image restoration, introduces degradation archetype representation and semantic/spatial ambiguity rectification modules to disentangle degradation cues from scene content, achieving state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing all-in-one image restoration methods encode heterogeneous degradations in a shared latent space, causing entanglement between degradation-related cues and scene content. This leads to dual ambiguity (semantic ambiguity in channel-wise modulation and spatial ambiguity in restoration responses), which can corrupt content and leave residual artifacts.
AI.method: DAR-Net consists of three components: (1) a Degradation Archetype Representation (DAR) module that constructs a structured degradation state via simplex-constrained archetype mixture modeling; (2) a Semantic Ambiguity Rectification (SeAR) module that generates degradation-aware prompts for improved channel-wise decoder conditioning; and (3) a Spatial Ambiguity Rectification (SpAR) module that regularizes degradation-aware and complementary features toward orthogonal response subspaces to reduce spatial interference.
AI.result: DAR-Net achieves the best overall performance on standard all-in-one restoration benchmarks under both three-degradation and five-degradation settings, improving average PSNR over the strongest competitor by 0.14 dB and 0.34 dB respectively, and shows superior performance on CDD-11 and WeatherBench.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly rectifying both semantic and spatial ambiguities through structured degradation state modeling and orthogonal feature regularization effectively disentangles degradation cues from scene content, yielding superior all-in-one image restoration performance.

title: PathView-Bench: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Achieve Fine-grained Multiscale Understanding of Pathology Images?
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to analyze pathology images.
